# Fidryn documentation

Fidryn (pronounced FID-rin) is a programming language for legal
instruments: precise where law is mechanical, explicit where judgment
enters, and incapable of hiding authority, discretion, or ambiguity
inside a Boolean.

This directory is the human documentation for the 0.3 reference
interpreter. Start at the [product README](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/README.md) to clone and
build, then read [Getting started](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started.md). The modules,
records, and examples in this repository are research fixtures. They
are not legal advice, not operative instruments, and not a complete
statement of any jurisdiction's law.

## For users

| Guide | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| [Getting started](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started.md) | First hour: build, `check`, `run` |
| [Language](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/language.md) | `.fr` modules, queries, rules, duties, verify |
| [Law modules](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md) | Law modules of edition 2, which hold provisions of law as data: the two editions, addresses and file paths, normalization, provisions, notes and layers, hashes, the syntax, what the checker verifies in one module, workspaces with their manifest and lock, how a workspace is checked and the outcome of each reference, the cache, definitions, curated modules with their names, dependencies and bindings, change sets, the ingester for the United States Code, the coverage ledger and the sample of the Code, and the limits |
| [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md) | Every `fidryn` subcommand and flag |
| [Mill](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md) | Localhost UI on 127.0.0.1 |
| [Cases and time](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md) | Case records, valid time, known-at |
| [Outcomes](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md) | Determinate, Suspended, Contingent, and the rest |
| [Examples](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/examples.md) | Trust, tax, federal slices, fifty states |
| [Coverage](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/coverage.md) | What the sample of the United States Code in the repository holds, in counts |

The closed grammar is [`grammar.ebnf`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/grammar.ebnf). Wire formats
are [`schemas/case-record-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/case-record-v0.1.json),
[`schemas/outcome-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/outcome-v0.1.json), and
[`schemas/evaluation-report-v0.2.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/evaluation-report-v0.2.json)
(CLI `run` / `explore` and mill eval responses nest the outcome as
`outcomeDocument`). The files of a workspace of law modules follow
[`schemas/workspace-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/workspace-v0.1.json),
[`schemas/law-lock-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/law-lock-v0.1.json) and
[`schemas/retrieval-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/retrieval-v0.1.json), the
coverage ledger of a generated workspace follows
[`schemas/coverage-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/coverage-v0.1.json), the
report of the check of a workspace follows
[`schemas/check-report-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/check-report-v0.1.json), the
text records that `fidryn text --json` prints follow
[`schemas/text-record-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/text-record-v0.1.json), and
the change set that `fidryn changes --json` prints follows
[`schemas/change-set-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/change-set-v0.1.json).

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started
> This markdown mirror is for agents and plain-text readers.

# Getting started with Fidryn

Clone the repository, install Rust 1.98, then check and run a tiny
`.fr` program. This is a first hour, not a complete encoding of any
jurisdiction.

Fidryn (FID-rin) is a programming language for legal instruments.
Source files use the `.fr` extension. A computation may return one
determinate result only when that result is invariant across every
still-admissible resolution of the unresolved issues, or when a
competent authority has already made a determination that is operative
in the relevant context. The interpreter never invents a completion.

This repository is the 0.3 research interpreter. The modules under
`examples/` and the programs under `tests/` are fixtures. They are not
legal advice, not operative instruments, and not a complete statement
of any jurisdiction's law.

From the repository root, every `fidryn` command below is written as
`cargo run -p fidryn-cli --` followed by its arguments, so it works
before you install a `fidryn` binary. After you install one, the same
arguments follow `fidryn`.

## Prerequisites

Install Rust 1.98. The workspace `rust-version` is 1.98.
[`rust-toolchain.toml`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/rust-toolchain.toml) pins the patch
(`1.98.1`) and the `rustfmt` / `clippy` components. `rustup` will pick
that toolchain up when you enter the repository.

You need a working C linker. On macOS, Command Line Tools clang is
enough.

## Build

From the repository root, compile the workspace and run the tests.
The first pass takes a bit: it builds every crate, then runs the
suite.

```sh
cargo test --workspace --locked
```

Confirm the CLI:

```sh
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- --help
```

You should see the `fidryn` subcommands, including `check` and `run`.
`run` evaluates a query against a case record and never chooses a
completion. See the [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md) guide for the rest of the surface.

## Check a tiny program

[`tests/programs/require-gate.fr`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/tests/programs/require-gate.fr)
is a complete module with two queries. `q` requires `true` and returns
`7`. `r` requires `false` and does not reach `return 7`.

```
module Programs.RequireGate version "0.1.0" {
    jurisdiction Test
    source_snapshot "2026-09-17-require-gate"
    effective_at 2026-09-17
    recorded_at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z

    outside_scope { complete_instruments }

    query q() -> Int { require true; return 7 }
    query r() -> Int { require false; return 7 }
}
```

Check it:

```sh
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- check tests/programs/require-gate.fr
```

Once `fidryn` is on your PATH, that is
`fidryn check tests/programs/require-gate.fr`. Success prints `ok`
and exits 0. Diagnostics go to stderr and the process exits 1.
`check` parses, elaborates, and type-checks. It does not evaluate a
query and does not need a case file.

## Run a query

`run` requires a case record plus both clocks. `--valid-at` is the
instant on the legal timeline you are asking about. `--known-at` is
the instant of the file you are willing to treat as known. Both are
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 (`Z` or a numeric offset). Use
`2026-09-17T12:00:00Z` for this hour. Details of the case JSON and
the two clocks are in [Cases and time](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md).

`require-gate` does not need facts or an interpretation. The repository ships
a minimal empty case record that satisfies the interchange schema
(`schema` and `admissibleCompletions` are the required properties), at
`tests/programs/cases/empty.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "fidryn.case-record/v0.1",
  "admissibleCompletions": {}
}
```

Run `q`. It should be determinate `7`:

```sh
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- run tests/programs/require-gate.fr \
    --query q \
    --case tests/programs/cases/empty.json \
    --valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z \
    --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z
```

The CLI prints one line of canonical JSON
(`fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2`). Pretty-printed, the important fields
look like this. This excerpt omits invocation hashes and derivation nodes; the
actual document also includes `invocation`, `invocationId`, `engineVersion`,
`sourceBundle` and `traceDocument`:

```json
{
  "schema": "fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2",
  "executionMode": "operative",
  "sourceTrust": "unauthenticated",
  "verificationMethod": "none",
  "assumptions": [],
  "coverage": null,
  "outcomeDocument": {
    "schema": "fidryn.outcome/v0.1",
    "module": "Programs.RequireGate@0.1.0",
    "query": "q",
    "asOf": {
      "validTime": "2026-09-17T12:00:00Z",
      "recordTime": "2026-09-17T12:00:00Z"
    },
    "modelBoundary": {
      "outsideScope": ["complete_instruments"],
      "admissibleCompletions": {
        "interpretations": {},
        "evidence": {},
        "choices": {}
      }
    },
    "outcome": {
      "kind": "determinate",
      "value": { "kind": "int", "data": 7 }
    }
  }
}
```

The six-kind legal result is nested under `outcomeDocument`.
`modelBoundary` is part of that answer. The module declared
`complete_instruments` as outside scope, so the envelope repeats that
exclusion. An omitted interpretation cannot silently shrink the model.
Pass `--scenario` only when you intend `case.assumptions` as an overlay;
operative `run` (the default) does not apply them. `--budget N` sets the maximum
number of evaluation operations; exhaustion is an engine error and cannot
produce a qualified determinate answer. The selected budget is part of the
invocation identity.

Save the complete report to retain its actual trace:

```text
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- run tests/programs/require-gate.fr --query q \
  --case tests/programs/cases/empty.json \
  --valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z > report.json
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- explain report.json --format text
```

`--source-root PATH` explicitly grants the filesystem root for artifacts and
packages. It defaults to the module directory; absolute paths, parent traversal
and symlinks cannot make an artifact escape that root.

Now run `r`:

```sh
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- run tests/programs/require-gate.fr \
    --query r \
    --case tests/programs/cases/empty.json \
    --valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z \
    --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z
```

`require false` does not skip ahead to `return 7`. Nested
`outcomeDocument.outcome` is `suspended`, with a request that the
requirement failed:

```json
{
  "outcomeDocument": {
    "outcome": {
      "kind": "suspended",
      "requests": [
        {
          "kind": "needCustom",
          "effect": "require",
          "payload": "requirement failed"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

That is the governing rule in miniature: the interpreter will not
pretend the later `7` is the answer. How those kinds compose is in
[Outcomes](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md).

`--query` is the query name as written in the module (`q`, `r`).
`--arg KEY=VALUE` writes `case.facts["KEY"]`. You do not need it here.

## Check a larger fixture

The Massachusetts trust fixture is a bounded slice of a private
instrument, not Massachusetts trust law as a whole. Check it the same
way:

```sh
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- check examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr
```

Success is again `ok`. The module lists `tax`, `creditor_priority`,
`real_property_recording`, and `complete_Massachusetts_trust_law` as
`outside_scope`. Those names will appear on `modelBoundary` if you
later `run` a query against a case under
[`examples/trust/cases/`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/tree/main/examples/trust/cases/).

The [examples](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/examples.md) catalog has more fixtures. They encode
bounded slices of the law. They do not contain the entire United
States Code.

## Next reading

1. [Language](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/language.md) — module headers, queries, rules, duties,
   and what Fidryn will not do.
2. [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md) — `check`, `run`, `explore`, and the other
   subcommands, with the flags the binary actually accepts.
3. [Outcomes](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md) — determinate, suspended, contingent, and
   the rest of the envelope.
4. [Cases and time](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md) — case JSON, admissible
   completions, `--valid-at` / `--known-at`.
5. [Examples](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/examples.md) — the fixture corpus under `examples/`.
6. [Mill](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md) — localhost `fidryn ui` on `127.0.0.1` (default
   port 8751). The mill checks a module in the browser. It does not
   live-file.

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/language
> This markdown mirror is for agents and plain-text readers.

# The Fidryn language

Read this as a map of the constructs you will see in `.fr` files, then
open the fixtures and check them. For build, `check`, and the first
`run`, start with [Getting started](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started.md).

Fidryn (FID-rin) is a language for legal instruments: precise where
law is mechanical, explicit where judgment enters. This repository is
the 0.3 research interpreter. Example modules are fixtures. They are
not legal advice, not operative instruments, and not a complete
statement of any jurisdiction's law.

The grammar in `grammar.ebnf` is closed, but the 0.3 parser enforces
that only inside `source` blocks, the bodies of rules and the request
block of a judgment's `otherwise suspend NeedJudgment`. In most other
declarations an unknown field is skipped without a diagnostic; see
[implementation status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md). Copy from an existing
`.fr` file when you are unsure a spelling parses. The reference is
[`grammar.ebnf`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/grammar.ebnf).

## Editions

A `.fr` file is of one of two editions. This guide describes the first,
which carries no marker: modules of queries, rules and the other
declarations below, which the interpreter checks and runs. A file whose
first two words are `edition 2`, before which only white space and
comments may stand, is a law module of edition 2: it holds provisions of
law as data in a grammar of its own, and it is checked and never
evaluated. Its reference is [Law modules](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md).

## Surface inventory (status-qualified)

The grammar ([`grammar.ebnf`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/grammar.ebnf)) is broader than this map.
Use the table as a honesty check; open a fixture for the full field list.
Support in 0.3 is **parsed / checked / executed** only where noted — see
[implementation-status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md).

| Construct | Fixture example | Status note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `import` (+ `digest` / `alias`) | `examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr` | Parsed. `alias` is accepted and ignored. An import with no digest and no matching package does nothing. |
| `record_type` / `evidence_type` | FOIA / trust fixtures | Parsed/checked; used as named evidence schemas |
| `observation` | LLC / state homestead modules | Parsed/checked; Observe matches schema + known-at |
| `scenario` | all 50 `examples/states/` modules | Name read; body not interpreted. Scenario runs use the case record's `assumptions`, not these blocks |
| `Evaluate` / `UniqueOccupant` / `RunDecision` / `StatusOf` | trust, late-payment, LLC | Executed query plans |
| `EvaluateClause` | `examples/prenup/ava-noah.fr` | Executed clause-plan queries |
| `power` / `legal_act` | trust, FOIA, prenup | Name and parameters read; body not interpreted, so unknown fields pass. A `legal_act` name types as a `LegalAction` in calls. Neither reaches evaluation |
| `clause` | prenup, minimum-wage | Name and parameters read; body kept as text. At run time only `EvaluateClause` uses it, and the evaluator knows two clause names |
| `conflict_doctrine` | prenup, minimum-wage | Body not interpreted; the text must name a declared clause after `defeat` (E511). Never consulted when staged effects disagree |
| `transaction` | `tests/programs/transaction-atomic.fr` | Partial; not a full commit engine |
| `for_all` / `exists` | status + grammar | Finite declared domains only; open domains suspend; no open-world proofs |
| `fn` | `packages/logic/true.fr` | Parsed, checked and executed; a query can call a function |
| Module type parameters | status | Type-name substitution only; no cross-file value-parameter calculus |

## Module header

Every file is one module. The header names the instrument, the dated
slice it encodes, and what it refuses to claim.

```
module Programs.LatePayment version "0.1.0" {
    jurisdiction Test
    source_snapshot "2026-09-17-late-payment"
    effective_at 2026-09-17
    recorded_at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z

    outside_scope { complete_instruments }

    // queries, duties, and interpretation families follow
}
```

`jurisdiction` is a name, not a choice of engine. `source_snapshot` is
the dated slice this file encodes. `effective_at` is a date.
`recorded_at` is a date-time (`Z` or a numeric offset).
`outside_scope` is a set of named exclusions; those names reappear on
the outcome's `modelBoundary`.

A comment begins with `//` and runs to the end of its line. There is no
block comment: `/* ... */` is read as ordinary tokens, not skipped.

A comment is never read as code. Whatever it holds, nothing is taken
from it: a `}` in a comment closes no block, a `->` begins no type, and
`assert false`, `defeat Residual` or `for_all x in People: true` in a
comment asserts nothing, defeats no clause and declares no property. A
comment at the end of a line of code does not change what that code
means. A line that holds only a comment is a blank line, and a blank
line is not always nothing: it can end a statement that the line below
would otherwise continue. See
[Where a statement ends](#where-a-statement-ends).

A bracket or a word inside a string literal is text of the string and
nothing else. `artifact "files/a}1.txt"` closes no block, a citation
such as `from "Stat. 12(a"` opens no parenthesis, and a string that holds
`defeat Residual` defeats no clause.

A comment can change text that is kept or shown as it is written, and
how a report identifies the program (see [outcomes](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md)), in
places such as these. `sourceBundle` covers the text of the module byte
for byte, so any comment changes it, and `fidryn review` shows the text
of each declaration with the comments inside it, but not a comment at
the end of its last line or one above it. `invocation.program.fingerprint`,
and with it `invocationId` and the trace ids, is taken over the compiled
program. That keeps some text as it is written: the body of a `clause`,
the first `assert` of a `verify` block, a line of a `verify` block that
is kept as an assertion that cannot be decided, and a clause of a
`judgment` or an `observation` that is kept as text. A comment inside
such text changes the fingerprint, as a change of the white space there
does. So does a comment at the end of the last line of such a kept
assertion or kept clause: the kept text then ends with the last token
before the comment, and with as many spaces in the comment's place it
ends with the spaces and the line end. The kept clauses of a judgment
are also quoted in the payload of its `JudgmentPolicy` request, in the
outcome of a run and in its trace. Those of an observation are quoted in
the error a run ends with when a record of the observed schema is on the
case, and in the output of `fidryn inputs`. A comment in such a clause,
or at the end of its last line, changes what these show. A comment at
the end of a line of a query, a rule or a duty, or at the end of the last
line of the first `assert` of a `verify` block, changes neither the
fingerprint nor the outcome of a run.

The trust fixture also declares a source manifest, resolved relative
to the module file:

```
source_manifest "sources/ma-trust-fixture.manifest.json"
```

A declared path that is missing or malformed is a diagnostic. Modules
that omit a manifest get an empty default. CLI `check` / `run` of a
path can byte-authenticate artifacts against files next to the module.
Pasted source in the [Mill](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md) does not.

## Sources and digests

A `source { }` block names an artifact the module is encoding.

```
source FinalPayStatute {
    kind statute
    authority CaliforniaLegislature
    citation "Cal. Lab. Code §§ 201-203"
    artifact "sources/ca-lab-201-203.txt"
    digest fixture
    effective [2026-09-17, +inf)
}
```

In 0.3 a `source` block is a record for the reader. The parser rejects
an unknown field in it, and the checker requires an `artifact` field
(`E540`). The checker also types the source's name as a `String`, so a
query that returns `FinalPayStatute` passes `check`, but `run` fails
with `unbound identifier`. Nothing else reads the block: it does not
reach evaluation, and the file named by `artifact` is never read,
whatever `digest` says ([implementation status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md)).

Digests are checked in the source manifest instead. That is the JSON
file the module names with `source_manifest`, or, when it names none,
`sources/manifest.json` or the only `*.manifest.json` in `sources/` next
to the module. Each manifest artifact has a `path` and a `digest`.
`"digest": "fixture"` is a fixture trust profile, not a hash of the file
and not byte verification. A 32- or 64-digit hex digest is blake3 of the
artifact bytes (64 hex: the full digest; 32 hex: the first 16 bytes).
`check` and `run` of a `.fr` path read the file at `path`, relative to
the module directory or to `--source-root`, and compare. A missing file
or a mismatch leaves the artifact unauthenticated, and an import that
requires that digest fails with E200. Pasted source in the
[Mill](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md) reads no manifest and no files.


## Imports

Modules may import another module by name and version. An import that
carries a `digest` must find that digest on an authenticated artifact of
the source manifest above, or the checker reports E200. An `alias` line
in an import is accepted and ignored in 0.3.

```
import MA.TrustLaw.Fixture version "2026-08-23"
import Agency.FOIARegulations version "fixture-2026-08-23" {
    digest fixture
}
```

In an import, `digest fixture` asks for a manifest artifact whose digest
is `fixture`. That is a trust profile, not byte verification. A hex
digest in an import asks for a manifest artifact with that digest whose
file `check` or `run` of a path has read and matched. With no matching
manifest artifact the import is E200. Mill paste loads no manifest, so
there an import with a digest is always E200.

## Entities, propositions, and offices

Name the parties and the propositions you will later test. A
proposition is not a Boolean.

```
entity Payer : NaturalPerson
entity Payee : NaturalPerson

proposition InvoiceIssued(person: NaturalPerson)
proposition Eligible(person: LegalPerson, office: Office)
```

An `office` is a position someone can occupy. From
[`examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr):

```
office TrusteeOf(trust: Trust) occupied_by LegalPerson {
    cardinality 0..1
    acquired_by Effective(AcceptOffice)
    suspended_by OperativeIncapacity
    lost_by {Death, EffectiveResignation, EffectiveRemoval}
    competence {AdministerTrust, DecideTrustDistributions}
}
```

Fidryn 0.3 reads only an office's name and parameters. The rest of the
declaration, `occupied_by` and every field in the body, is discarded:
every office reaches the intermediate representation with occupant type
`LegalPerson`, at most one occupant and no competence, and nothing reads
the declaration at run time (test
`an_office_keeps_none_of_its_declared_fields`; see
[implementation status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md)).

`Occupies(Bryan, TrusteeOf(BRT))` is a proposition about that office,
not a `Bool`.


## Record and evidence types

Name structured payloads the case and Observe paths will carry.

```
record_type FOIARequest {
    // fields as in examples/foia/foia-request.fr
}

evidence_type PhysicianCertificate {
    // fields as in examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr
}
```

These declarations are part of the closed grammar. Copy field shapes from
an existing fixture rather than inventing spellings.

## Observations

An `observation` names an evidence-shaped fact the evaluator may Observe.
Its header binds one record and, after `establishes`, gives the
proposition that the record establishes. Its body holds the conditions
the record must meet. This one is from
[`examples/tax/federal-tax.fr`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/examples/tax/federal-tax.fr):

```
observation DomesticFormationRecord(record: BeneficialOwnershipReport)
establishes DomesticCompany(record.company)
    from FinCENBOIFinalRule.section("domestic-entity")
{
    require record.company == AcmeLLC
}
```

A header with no `establishes` or with no `{ ... }` body is rejected with
`E100`.

Observe still requires a matching case evidence row with `observedAt` at
or before `--known-at`. Declaring an observation does not invent the
record.

## Queries, goals, and effects

A query is the thing you `run`. The body is `return` / `require`
statements or an explicit `goal`. Fixtures use `Evaluate`,
`UniqueOccupant`, `RunDecision`, and `StatusOf`.

```
query due() -> Money<USD> {
    goal Evaluate { USD(100.00) }
}

query acting_trustee() -> LegalPerson ! {Observe, Determine, Interpret} {
    goal UniqueOccupant { office TrusteeOf(BRT) }
}

query paid_on_time() -> Bool ! {Observe} {
    goal RunDecision { decision TimelyPayment }
}

query entity_status() -> EntityStatus ! {Observe, Determine} {
    goal StatusOf {
        status FormedLLC(HarborRobotics)
        when_present FormedLLC(HarborRobotics)
        when_closed_absent NotFormedLLC(HarborRobotics)
    }
}
```

`Evaluate` computes a term. `UniqueOccupant` asks who occupies an
office. `RunDecision` runs a named `decision` against the case.
`StatusOf` reports a legal status when present, or the closed-absent
form when the domain is closed
([`harbor-robotics.fr`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/examples/massachusetts-llc/harbor-robotics.fr)).

`EvaluateClause` is an additional query plan used by some instruments
(for example [`examples/prenup/ava-noah.fr`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/examples/prenup/ava-noah.fr)):

```
query provision_result() -> ... ! {Observe, Determine, Interpret} {
    goal EvaluateClause {
        // clause plan
    }
}
```

The effect row `! {Observe, Determine, Interpret}` is permission, not
a promise that the engine will invent evidence. If the case does not
supply what the effect needs, the outcome is `suspended`. `run` never
fills that request. See [Outcomes](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md) and
[Cases and time](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md).

## Automatic versus judgment

Mark a query `automatic` only when the answer is mechanical and the
effect row is empty.

```
query automatic pay_due_immediately(discharged: Bool) -> Bool {
    return discharged
}

query waiting_time_penalty() -> Bool ! {Determine} {
    goal Evaluate {
        require determined WillfulFailureToPay(Employer)
            using Determine
        return true
    }
}
```

The waiting-time query answers `true` once the case records a
determination that establishes `WillfulFailureToPay(Employer)`. It
suspends otherwise, including when the determination is negative (tests
`an_established_determination_makes_the_judgment_query_true` and
`a_negative_determination_suspends_and_never_answers_false` in
`tests/integration/repaired_examples.rs`).

An automatic query that reaches `Determine`, `Observe`, or `Interpret`
is E420. Willful failure is a judgment, not a Bool you compute in the
module. The waiting-time query is allowed to suspend.

A `judgment` declaration names who decides a proposition, what record
it needs, and what happens on established / rejected / otherwise. The
trust fixture's incapacity judgment requires two distinct physician
certificates and otherwise suspends `NeedJudgment`. The language will
not collapse "the physicians have not spoken" into `false`.

## Require, return, and sequential evaluation

Statements in a block run left to right. Several statements lower to
a `seq`; the last value is the result. `require` is a gate: `true`
continues, `false` suspends and does not return the later value.

```
query q() -> Int { require true; return 7 }
query r() -> Int { require false; return 7 }
```

`q` is determinate `7`. `r` is `suspended` (`needCustom` /
`requirement failed`). That is why [Getting started](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started.md)
runs both. Nested `seq` under `+`, a call, or `if` resumes by skipping
the completed prefix, so a later term does not re-run an earlier
attach.

`require determined P using Determine` asks for a determination of `P`
instead of treating `P` as a Bool. In 0.3 the `using` clause is parsed
and discarded. Any determination of `P` on the case that names a
protocol and a decider answers the requirement. A negative determination
fails it, and with none the query suspends with a request for a judgment
on `P`. The protocol name stands in the statement of `using`: a `using`
that ends its statement, with no name after it, is rejected with `E100`,
and the line below it is not read as the name.

A statement that a query body, a `goal Evaluate` block, the body of a
`calc` or an `fn`, or a `transaction` block cannot read is rejected with
`E100`, wherever it stands in the block. A `return` with no expression is
one.

## Where a statement ends

A statement ends at a `;` or at the end of its line. It goes on into the
next line in two cases.

- The line ends in a token that cannot end a statement. The tokens that
  can are a name or word, a literal, `)`, `]`, `}`, `*` and `>`. A line
  that ends in one of the prefix words `not`, `operative`, `effective`,
  `established`, `determined`, `always`, `active`, `every`, `unique` and
  `closed` goes on as well.
- The next line begins with a continuation: one of the words `and`, `or`,
  `in`, `where`, `then`, `else`, `from`, `decides`, `occupied_by`,
  `establishes`, `using`, `for`, `rank`, `as`, `to`, `version` and `fuel`,
  or one of the tokens `.`, `,`, `->`, `=>`, `:`, `=`, `|`, `<`, `!`, `{`,
  `(` and `[`.

A blank line has no token, and neither has a line that holds only a
comment. The first case holds across such lines. The second holds across
them only for a line that begins with `and`, `or`, `in`, `.`, `,`, `->`,
`=>`, `:`, `=`, `|` or `<`. No statement begins with one of those, so a
condition can carry a comment between its lines:

```
rule BothConditions : derive from "cite" {
    when operative A
        // the second condition
        and operative B
    then derive C
}
```

The guard of that rule is `operative A and operative B`. Each of the
other continuations, such as `then`, `for` or `(`, can begin a statement
of its own, so below a blank line or a comment line it does not continue
the statement above. That holds where the parser tests whether a
statement has ended, as it does after the condition of an `if` and after
the word `else`: the block of a branch does not stand below a blank line
or a comment line. In some places where it expects the next part of a form
it does not test, and reads on across blank and comment lines: an `else`
after the block of an `if`, for example, and the `{ ... }` block that
follows the domain of a quantifier or the word `transaction`.

Parentheses, brackets and braces do not change the rule: a line break
inside them ends the expression before it in the same cases. `(1`
followed by the line `+ 2)` is rejected, because `+` is not a
continuation. Write `(1 +` and then `2)`.

Text the parser steps over without reading it, such as a `verify` field
it does not read or a clause it keeps as text, ends by the same rule with
three differences. A line break inside its parentheses, brackets or
braces does not end it. A prefix word at the end of a line does not carry
it into the next line. And it ends after the `}` that closes its
outermost brace, unless a continuation follows.

A declaration does not go on into the declaration below it. Outside the
parentheses, brackets and braces that a declaration has opened and not
closed, a line that begins with a declaration keyword is no part of that
declaration, whatever the line above it ends in. Blank lines and comment
lines between the two change nothing. There is one exception: below the
header of a `for_all` or an `exists` that ends in `:`, a line that begins
with `for_all` or `exists` is the body of the quantifier.

So the first case above does not carry a header into such a line. A
header that leaves no bracket open and whose line ends in `,`, `.`, `:`,
`!`, `->`, `=>`, `=`, `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>=`, `+`, `-`, `/`, `|` or
`..` is not finished above such a line, and the module is rejected with
`E100`: `rule R : derive from Basis +` above the line `clause C {` is
rejected, and `clause C` is a declaration with its own block. That holds
wherever in a header the token stands: after an operator that lacks its
operand, after a name that ends in `.`, after the `!` of an effect row,
among type arguments that `<` opens and no `>` closes, and after the `:`,
`->` or `=` that a type follows. A prefix word at the end of the `from`
basis of a rule, or of an expression in the header of a judgment or an
observation, lacks its operand in the same way: the module is rejected
with `E100`, and the declaration below is read. A type on the next line
that is no declaration keyword is read: `entity Pat :` followed by the
line `NaturalPerson` declares `Pat`. Inside a bracket that the
declaration has left open, the lines below can still be read as what the
bracket holds: below `proposition P(`, the line `clause C {` is read as a
parameter, and the module is rejected with no clause declared.

A keyword that takes a name, such as `entity`, `rule` or `query`, is
rejected with `E100` when its statement ends with it: the name is not
read from the next line. It is rejected as well when the token after it
is not a name, as in `power { holder A }` or `entity : NaturalPerson`.
The six header keywords, `jurisdiction`, `source_snapshot`,
`source_manifest`, `effective_at`, `recorded_at` and `outside_scope`, are
rejected with `E100` in the same way when the statement ends with the
keyword: the value is not read from the next line.

## Calc, conditionals, money, and durations

`calc` is a total, effect-free function. It must not recurse (E530).

```
calc return_deadline() -> Duration<counted_days> {
    return 21 counted_days
}

calc federal_hourly_floor() -> Money<USD> {
    return USD(7.25)
}
```

A `calc` or an `fn` needs its `{ ... }` body. A header with none is
rejected with `E100`.

Fidryn 0.3 cannot add a duration to a time in an expression: `end +
return_deadline()`, with `end: Time`, is `E210`. A deadline is computed
only by a duty's `due` clause; see [Duties](#duties).

Money is `USD(100.00)`, never an untyped decimal. Durations carry a
calendar kind (`counted_days`, `calendar_days`, `working_days`,
`days`, `hours`, `minutes`, `seconds`). `21 counted_days` and `21 days`
have different types, but a duty's `due` clause counts each of them as
21 days of 24 hours.

`if` / `else` is Boolean control flow. The condition must be a `Bool`,
not a proposition. [`prelude/tax.fr`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/prelude/tax.fr) uses it on
amounts:

```
if amount <= 11925.00 {
    amount * 0.10
} else {
    if amount <= 48475.00 {
        11925.00 * 0.10 + (amount - 11925.00) * 0.12
    } else {
        if amount <= 103350.00 {
            11925.00 * 0.10 + (48475.00 - 11925.00) * 0.12 + (amount - 48475.00) * 0.22
        } else {
            17651.00 + (amount - 103350.00) * 0.24
        }
    }
}
```

The `{` after the condition opens the branch. In the condition of an
`if`, in the domain of a quantifier, and in the header of a rule, a
judgment or an observation, a name followed by `{` is therefore the name
alone and is not applied to the block: `if flag { 1 } else { 2 }` tests
`flag`. A record constructor written with its name needs parentheses
there, as in `if (R { x: 1 }) == r { 1 } else { 2 }`.

An `if` or an `else` needs its branch in the same statement. With none,
the module is rejected with `E100`.

This is a rejected guard (E310):

```
query bad() -> LegalPerson {
    goal Evaluate { if Incapacitated(Bryan) { Bryan } }
}
```

Use `when operative P` on a rule, or `require determined P using
Determine` in a query. `Prop` has no conversion to `Bool`.

## Rules

A `rule` fires when a guard holds, then derives or establishes a
proposition. The current staged worklist is **bounded and specialized**
([implementation-status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md)); this is not a
general rule engine, and prescriptive duties / full transaction commit
are not that worklist. The kind is `derive`, `constitutive`, or `prescriptive`.

```
rule InitialTrustee : constitutive
    from Instrument.clause("1.2")
{
    when operative TrustInstrumentExecuted(BRT) in TrustCreation(BRT)
    then establish Occupies(Bryan, TrusteeOf(BRT))
}
```

The `from` basis can also be a bare name, as in `from Instrument`: the `{`
after it opens the rule's body. A rule needs that body. A rule header
with no `{ ... }` after it is rejected with `E100`.

The body holds `when`, `then`, `otherwise`, `require`, `select` and
`source` statements. Other text in it is rejected with `E100`, and so is
a `then` or an `otherwise` that no consequence follows, and a `when`, a
`require` or a `source` with no expression after it. A consequence names
a proposition: `then establish 5` is rejected with `E210`, and so is a
consequence that is the name of an entity whose type is neither `Prop`
nor an alias of `Prop`. Two more lines are accepted:
`valid_time` and `record_time`, each followed by an interval with both of
its bounds, such as `[2026-08-14, +inf)`. Fidryn 0.3 reads them and does
not apply them: the consequences of the rule hold at every time, whatever
the interval says (see
[implementation-status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md#known-limits-pinned-by-tests)).

`when operative P` tests legal status. `in TrustCreation(BRT)` names the
legal context of that test. The guard still turns on the proposition
`TrustInstrumentExecuted(BRT)`. It is not a proposition named `in`.
`when determined P` tests for a determination of `P` already on the case.
`then derive` and `then establish` are the usual consequences. Guards
must use `operative`, `determined`, `assumed`, or `necessarily` — not a
bare proposition. The successor rule in the trust fixture also
`select unique candidate from nominations_for(...)` with
`require unique nomination_rank`. A tie is not a silent pick.

## Interpretation families

When the instrument still admits more than one reading, declare the
family and what each alternative establishes.

```
interpretation_family DeadlineMeaning {
    alternative Strict {
        defines GracePeriod(0) as established
        defines StrictDeadline() as established
        defines ExtendedDeadline() as not_established
    }
    alternative Extended {
        defines GracePeriod(15) as established
        defines StrictDeadline() as not_established
        defines ExtendedDeadline() as established
    }
}
```

Each `defines P as established` or `defines P as not_established` is
a claim in that world. The case lists still-admissible alternatives
under `admissibleCompletions.interpretations`. `run` does not pick
`Strict` because it is written first. If the query needs a reading
and the case has not selected one, the outcome is `suspended`
(`needInterpretation`).

The trust fixture binds a family to a clause and names a selector
(`explicit_instrument_definition or controlling_interpretation or
request Interpret`). That is how a court selection on the case becomes
operative. It is not a default vote.

## Nominations

A nomination is a ranked candidate for an office.

```
nomination Alice for TrusteeOf(BRT) rank 1
    from Instrument.clause("4.4.a")

nomination Bob for TrusteeOf(BRT) rank 2
    from Instrument.clause("4.4.b")
```

Rank `1` is higher than rank `2`. Duplicate ranks for the same office
are E410. Rank is not occupancy: `UniqueOccupant` still needs an
occupancy record, eligibility, and any required acceptance. Open
eligibility stays `suspended`, or becomes `contingent` under
[CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md) `explore` with declared bounds. It does not collapse to
the first name on the list.


## Powers, legal acts, clauses, and conflict doctrines

These constructs appear in fixtures (trust, FOIA, prenup, minimum wage).

```
power SettlorAmendmentPower { ... }
legal_act AcceptOffice(candidate: LegalPerson, office: Office) { ... }
conflict_doctrine ChildSupportCannotBeAdverselyAffected ...
```

Fidryn 0.3 does not interpret the bodies of `power`, `legal_act`,
`conflict_doctrine` or `scenario` declarations, so an unknown field in
one of them passes without a diagnostic. A `clause` body is kept as text.
The evaluator knows two clause names, `SpousalSupportWaiver` and
`ChildSupportWaiver`; see [implementation status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md).

When the rules' staged effects both add and withdraw the same
proposition, the outcome kind is `normConflict`. No `conflict_doctrine`
is consulted, and list order is never a silent tie-break.

## Duties

A `duty` names bearer, claimant, attachment, content, and due time.
From [`tests/programs/late-payment.fr`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/tests/programs/late-payment.fr):

```
duty PayInvoice {
    bearer Payer
    claimant Payee
    attaches when operative InvoiceIssued(Payer)
    content USD(100.00)
    due 0 counted_days after invoice_date
}

query obligation_status() -> DutyState {
    goal Evaluate {
        duty_status(PayInvoice)
    }
}
```

`duty_status(Name)` looks up that duty declaration plus the case on the
**implemented specialized duty path** (see late-payment fixtures and
[implementation-status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md)). It does not invent
performance and is not a general legal-duty / transaction engine. Status is one of `Unresolved`,
`Attached`, `Performed`, `Breached`, `Cured`, `Discharged`. A late
perform can remain `Performed` with `breached: true`. Changing
`due 0 counted_days` to `due 15 counted_days` changes when the same
case becomes `Breached`; see `late-payment-extended.fr`.

Declaring a duty does not attach it. Attachment waits on the `when`
guard. A `kind: duty` event on the case does not commit performance
unless an authority grant covers the action, or the event is an
explicit `assumption`. That gate is in
[Cases and time](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md).


## Transactions and quantifiers

`transaction { ... }` blocks exist in the grammar and are exercised by
`tests/programs/transaction-atomic.fr`. Support is **partial** — not a
full atomic commit engine for arbitrary legal acts.

`for_all` / `exists` quantify over **finite declared domains** (and
closures where required). The body follows the domain after a `:` or as a
block: `for_all x in Scores: x > 0` and `for_all x in Scores { x > 0 }`
are the same quantifier. Open domains suspend. Nested / open-world
theorem proving is not implemented. Prefer reading
[implementation-status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md) before treating a
quantified `verify` as a proved theorem.

## Scenarios (in-module)

A `scenario` block writes down example hypotheses in fixtures that do
not ship companion JSON case files (for example under
`examples/states/`).

```
scenario InsideCityHalfAcre {
    assume OccupiesAsResidence(Owner, Home)
    assume InsideMunicipality(Home)
    assume within_urban_acreage(0.5)
    at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00
}
```

Grammar: `ScenarioDecl` in [`grammar.ebnf`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/grammar.ebnf). Fidryn
0.3 does not interpret a `scenario` block: the parser reads its name and
skips its body, and nothing in it reaches evaluation
([implementation status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md)). Neither `run` nor
`run --scenario` reads these blocks.

Scenario evaluation is driven by the case record. Its `assumptions`
rows (`id`, `payload`) are applied when you pass `run --scenario`, and
the report's `executionMode` is then `scenario`. The mill uses scenario
mode when the pasted case has a nonempty `assumptions` list. A default
`run` is operative and ignores `assumptions`. See
[Cases and time](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md) and [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md).

## Verify

A `verify` block is a named property made of `assert` lines. Fidryn 0.3
decides closed formulas only: literals, arithmetic, comparisons, Boolean
connectives, and quantifiers over a literal set or bounded synthetic
entities.

```
verify Arithmetic {
    assert true
    assert 1 + 1 == 2
}
```

Both assertions hold, so the property is proved. A false assertion, such
as `assert false` or `assert 1 + 1 == 3`, is a counterexample. An
assertion that cannot be decided without a query or a proposition is
unresolved, and the property is then `unknown` unless another assertion
is false. For those properties,

```text
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- verify PATH --property NAME
```

reports `unknown` rather than pretending they are theorems. Fixture
modules often write honesty properties in English-shaped `assert`
lines (`assert automatic pay_due_immediately has empty effect row`).
Treat those as documentation the checker records as a verify item, not
as a solved proof. The empty-effect-row rule for `automatic` is E420
whether or not a `verify` block repeats it.

### The fields of a verify block

A verify block is a list of fields. Nine words begin a field:

| First word | What `verify` does with the field |
| --- | --- |
| `assert` | The expression after it is an assertion. |
| `for_all`, `exists` | The expression the word begins is an assertion, checked in the same way. |
| `bounds` | It is read for three numbers, the synthetic persons, events and time points, and for nothing else. |
| `interpretations`, `judgments`, `choices`, `assuming` | The field is recognized and not read. |
| `for` | A `for every` line is not evaluated. It is kept as an assertion that cannot be decided. |

An assertion that cannot be decided leaves the property `unknown` unless
another assertion is false. A block with no assertion is `unknown` too,
whatever its comments say: a comment is never read as an assertion.

The bounds come from a `bounds` field and from nowhere else. Each of the
three numbers is read at the first place where its word, `persons`,
`events` or `time_points`, stands as a token in the field. When the next
token is an integer, or a `:` followed by an integer, that integer is the
number. Otherwise the number is zero, as it is when the word is not in the
field. So `bounds persons x persons 2` gives zero persons, and so do
`persons: 2.5`, which is not an integer, and an integer that does not fit
in 32 bits.

No comment sets a number, wherever it stands: inside the field, after it
on its line, or on the lines below it. The contents of a string are not
read either. Another field that holds the word `bounds` does not set the
bounds, and a block with no `bounds` field has zero of each. When a block
has several `bounds` fields, the last one counts. The test
`the_bounds_come_only_from_a_bounds_field` in
`tests/integration/verify_blocks.rs` pins each of these rules.

A field ends where its statement ends; see
[Where a statement ends](#where-a-statement-ends). An `assert`, `for_all`,
`exists` or `bounds` field, and a field that is not read, ends earlier
where the next field begins, as if a `;` stood there:

- The word `assert` begins a field wherever it stands, in the middle of a
  line too.
- A line that begins with one of the other eight words begins a field. In
  the middle of a line those words do not cut a field short:
  `assuming fair for every x in {1, 2}: x == 3` is one `assuming` field,
  and none of it is read.
- There is one exception. Below an `assert`, `for_all` or `exists` field,
  a line that begins with `for_all` or `exists` does not end that field.
  It continues the line above when the statement goes on into it, and is
  a field of its own when the statement has ended. This is one assertion,
  and it is proved:

  ```
  verify EveryNumberHasAnEqual {
      for_all x in {1, 2}:
          exists y in {1, 2}: x == y
  }
  ```

- Nothing inside the parentheses, brackets or braces of a field begins a
  field.

A `for every` line, and a line the block does not recognize, have no
early end. The parser steps over such a line as text it does not read,
together with every line that text goes on into, an `assert` line
included, and the whole is one assertion that cannot be decided.

An expression that is complete where the next field begins is an
assertion. One that is cut off there gets the diagnostic it would get
before a `;`: `assert true or 1 +` followed by the line `assert false` is
rejected with `E100`, "expected expression after operator", and
`assert if true { true } else` followed by the line `assert true` is
rejected with `E100`, "expected `{` after `else`". Where the parser has no
diagnostic before a `;`, there is none here either: `not` with nothing
after it gives no expression. An `assert` with no expression, `assert not`
included, is an assertion that cannot be decided.

Text that follows the expression of an `assert`, `for_all` or `exists`
field is read as the next field when it begins with one of the nine
words. That is rare on one line, because a word that directly follows an
expression is normally taken into the expression as an operand:
`assert true assuming fair` is one assertion, and it cannot be decided.
Before a `:` or an `=` a word is not an operand, so
`assert true assuming: x` is the assertion `true` followed by an
`assuming` field.

Text that begins with none of the nine words, such as a misspelled
`assert`, is not dropped either. When the field above goes on into it, it
is part of that field. Otherwise it is read as a line of its own and kept
as an assertion that cannot be decided, with one difference after an
`assert`: the `assert` and the text that follows its expression, on the
same line or below it, are together one assertion that cannot be decided,
and the module is rejected with `E100` when that text begins with
something other than a word.

Two limits remain.

- What stands inside the parentheses, brackets or braces of a `bounds`
  field, or of a field that is not read, belongs to that field, and so
  does a line that begins with none of the nine words when the field goes
  on into it. None of it is read as an assertion: an `assert false`
  between the braces of an `interpretations` field or of a `bounds` field
  is not read.
- `verify` evaluates an assertion; it does not type-check it. A true
  operand of `or` and a false operand of `and` settle the result whatever
  the other operand is, and the branch an `if` does not take is not
  examined. So `assert true or no_such_name` is proved, and so is
  `assert true or 1 +` followed by the line
  `for_all x in {1, 2}: x == 3`, where the second line is the right
  operand of `+`.

## What the language will not do

Fidryn will not hide judgment in a `Bool`. A proposition is a `Prop`.
`if Incapacitated(Bryan)` is E310. Write `operative`, `determined`,
`assumed`, or `necessarily`, or request `Determine`.

Fidryn will not invent a completion. `run` evaluates the case you
supplied. Missing interpretation, evidence, or choice yields
`suspended`. An empty admissible set is `inconsistent` or
`suspended`, never a vacuous determinate answer. `explore` searches
only the finite domains you declared.

Fidryn will not treat `Prop` as `Bool`. `defines Eligible(Alice,
TrusteeOf(BRT)) as not_established` is not `false`. It is a reading of
a proposition in one named alternative.

Those three refusals are the language. The [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md) will not
choose a completion either. The [examples](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/examples.md) show the
refusals in larger fixtures. The [Mill](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md) will not live-file.

========== https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md ==========

---
title: "Cases and time"
description: "Case records, admissible completions, valid-at and known-at in Fidryn."
url: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time"
markdown: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md"
author: "Bryan Gass"

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time
> This markdown mirror is for agents and plain-text readers.

# Cases and time

This guide explains how to supply a case record to Fidryn. Fidryn is a
research interpreter for legal instruments. It is not legal advice, not an
operative filing system, and not a statement of any jurisdiction's law.
The JSON you write is a fixture for evaluation, not a court record.

A case is a `fidryn.case-record/v0.1` document. The interchange schema is
[`schemas/case-record-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/case-record-v0.1.json). Wire
names are camelCase except where a nested type keeps its Rust field names
(determinations use `recorded_at`).

Required properties are `schema` and `admissibleCompletions`. Everything
else may be omitted and defaults to empty. The published schema lists
`schema`, `module`, `facts`, `evidence`, `determinations`,
`interpretations`, `decisions`, `closures`, `outsideScope`, and
`admissibleCompletions`. The interpreter also reads `events` and
`assumptions` when present; those fields are not yet in
[`schemas/case-record-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/case-record-v0.1.json)
(`additionalProperties` is false there). Treat that published schema lag
as an evidence gap in
[implementation-status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md), not as CLI behavior.

## Supplying a case

Pass a JSON file to `fidryn run` or `fidryn explore`:

```text
fidryn run PATH --query NAME --case RECORD.json --valid-at TIME --known-at TIME \
    [--arg KEY=VALUE] [--scenario] [--budget N]
fidryn explore PATH --query NAME --case RECORD.json [--bounds BOUNDS.json] \
    --valid-at TIME --known-at TIME
```

`TIME` is ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 with a `Z` suffix or a numeric offset
(`2033-01-01T00:00:00Z`, `2033-01-01T00:00:00+00:00`). Equal instants
canonicalize to UTC. `run` never chooses a missing completion. `--arg
KEY=VALUE` writes `case.facts["KEY"]`. `--scenario` evaluates with
`case.assumptions` as an overlay. `explore --bounds` merges extra
declared domains into `admissibleCompletions`. Successful `run` /
`explore` stdout is `fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2`.

See [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md), the [language grammar](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/grammar.ebnf), and
[Outcomes](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md).

## Assumptions and scenario evaluation

`Assumption` rows are `{ "id": "...", "payload": ... }`. They are overlay
hypotheses, not operative ledger events.

- CLI `run` without `--scenario` is **operative**: `case.assumptions` are
  ignored for evaluation.
- CLI `run --scenario` applies those rows as a scenario overlay and labels
  the report `executionMode: scenario` (assumptions are serialized on the
  evaluation-report envelope).
- Mill `/api/run` and `/api/explore` have no `--scenario` flag; a nonempty
  `assumptions` array selects the scenario path automatically.

The published interchange schema
[`schemas/case-record-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/case-record-v0.1.json) does
not yet list `events` or `assumptions` (`additionalProperties` is false).
The interpreter still reads both when present. Treat that as schema lag /
an implementation extension documented in
[implementation-status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md), not as proof that the
fields are invalid at runtime.

## Record shape

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | Must be the string `fidryn.case-record/v0.1`. |
| `module` | Optional module identity (`Name@version`). The outcome envelope uses the compiled module, not this string, as `sourceSnapshot`. |
| `facts` | Named values already treated as given. Bare JSON booleans, integers, and strings are accepted. |
| `evidence` | Observed records. Each item has `schema`, `value`, and `observedAt`. |
| `determinations` | Competent judgments already on file. Nested fields are `issue`, `protocol`, `established`, `decider`, and optional `recorded_at`. |
| `interpretations` | Selected alternative per interpretation family (`"SuccessorEligibility": "I2"`). |
| `decisions` | Selected option per choice protocol. |
| `closures` | Closed-world flags (`domain`, `closed`). Absence is not a determinate negative unless the domain is closed. |
| `admissibleCompletions` | The declared finite model. This is the model boundary, not a hint. |
| `outsideScope` | Named exclusions. The outcome envelope unions these with the module's `outside_scope`. |
| `events` | Optional ledger rows (`kind`, `validTime`, `recordTime`, `payload`). |
| `assumptions` | Optional overlay hypotheses (`id`, `payload`). Not operative case state. CLI `run --scenario` applies them; mill `/api/run` and `/api/explore` treat a nonempty list as scenario mode. Default `run` without `--scenario` leaves them unused. |

`admissibleCompletions` has three maps:

```json
"admissibleCompletions": {
  "interpretations": {
    "SuccessorEligibility": ["I1", "I2"]
  },
  "evidence": {
    "SecondConcurringCertificate": {
      "responses": ["absent", "present_prospective"],
      "effectOnValidTime": "unchanged_if_after_query_valid_time"
    }
  },
  "choices": {
    "DistributionProtocol": ["hold", "distribute"]
  }
}
```

`interpretations` maps a family name to the alternatives the instrument
still admits. `evidence` maps a schema name to a finite response list
and an optional `effectOnValidTime`. `choices` maps a protocol name to
the options a decision-maker may still pick.

That object is the model. An omitted family is not silently filled in
later. An empty declared list for a named family is not a vacuous
determinate world: explore treats it as an empty completion set
(`inconsistent`), even if `interpretations` already records a selection.
A recorded alternative that is not in the declared list is outside
competence, not a new world.

## Valid time and record time

Fidryn is bitemporal. Every evaluation has two clocks.

`--valid-at` is valid time: the instant on the legal timeline you are
asking about (when occupancy, a deadline, or a status is supposed to
hold). `--known-at` is record time: the instant of the file you are
willing to treat as known. Occupancy and similar ledgers must contain
the valid instant and must have been recorded no later than record time.

These clocks are independent. You can ask what the office was on
2026-08-23 using only records known on that day, or you can ask the same
valid-time question using a later known-at that includes subsequent
filings.

The outcome envelope repeats the pair as `asOf.validTime` and
`asOf.recordTime`.

## Evidence after known-at does not count

Each evidence item carries `observedAt`. Observe matches schema, the
issue's subject when the value designates one, and `observedAt <=
--known-at`. A certificate dated after known-at is invisible to that
query. It does not become a determinate negative; the query still
suspends if the remaining known record is incomplete.

The same cutoff applies to duty and institutional events: `recordTime`
after known-at is not admitted.

Determinations match **protocol and issue**. `established: false` is a
negative determination from a competent authority, not
`outsideCompetence`. A determination for Alice does not discharge a
judgment about Bob.

## Completions are the model boundary

`run` evaluates the case you gave. If an interpretation, choice, or
judgment is required and missing, the outcome is `suspended` with a
`needInterpretation`, `needChoice`, or `needJudgment` request. `run`
does not pick I1 because it is listed first.

`explore` searches the **declared** completions. Recorded selections
constrain that search: a case that already records
`SuccessorEligibility: I2` is not re-opened onto I1. Declared evidence
responses such as `absent` versus `present_prospective` are hypothetical
worlds for explore, not facts invented by `run`.

Three different empty-looking objects are not the same:

- `"admissibleCompletions": {}` declares no open families. A query that
  does not need an interpretation can still be determinate.
- `"interpretations": {}` on the case means no alternative has been
  selected yet. If the query needs one, `run` suspends.
- `"admissibleCompletions": { "interpretations": { "Family": [] } }`
  declares a family whose admissible set is empty. That is not a
  determinate answer by vacuity. Explore reports `inconsistent` with
  core `empty completion set`. A recorded selection cannot reopen that
  empty domain.

Interpretations you record must be members of the declared domain for
that family. `I2` is lawful only when `I2` appears in
`admissibleCompletions.interpretations.SuccessorEligibility`. An
off-list selection is `outsideCompetence` (`recorded interpretation is
not in the admissible set` / `inadmissible interpretation`). The same
rule applies to `decisions` versus `choices`.

## Money and structured values

Case JSON accepts bare literals for booleans, integers, and strings.
Decimals and other runtime values must be tagged so they do not alias
those literals.

```json
{ "kind": "decimal", "data": "1.25" }
```

is money-as-decimal. The bare string `"1.25"` is a string. A JSON
number that is not an integer may decode as decimal, but do not rely on
that for amounts you care about: write the tagged form.

```json
{ "kind": "bool", "data": false }
```

is the boolean false.

```json
{ "kind": "record", "data": { "kind": "bool", "data": false } }
```

is a user record whose fields happen to be named `kind` and `data`.
Without the `record` wrapper, `{"kind":"bool","data":false}` is always
boolean, so you cannot store a complaint-shaped object that uses those
field names as a tagged bool. Unknown `kind` tags (for example
`{"kind":"Complaint","id":"1"}`) decode as a map, not as a bool.

Other tagged forms you may need:

```json
{ "kind": "entity", "data": "Alice" }
{ "kind": "instant", "data": "2026-08-23T12:00:00Z" }
{ "kind": "prop", "data": { "predicate": "Incapacitated", "arguments": [] } }
```

A bare `"Alice"` is a string, not an entity. A proposition is never a
boolean; see [Outcomes](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md).

## Authority grants and duty events

Institutional events do not commit performance just because they appear
in JSON. Events with `kind` `duty`, `authority`, or `institutional` are
admitted only when an `AuthorityGrant` covers the action at
`recordTime`. Assumptions are explicit: `kind` `assumption` skips that
gate.

Grants may be evidence:

```json
{
  "schema": "AuthorityGrant",
  "value": { "action": "perform" },
  "observedAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

or a fact named `authority_grants`. A `duty` event whose payload is
`Performed` / `action: "perform"` without a covering grant is dropped
from the duty machine. It does not turn `duty_status` into Performed.

`kind` `evidence` rows are copied onto the record ledger at
`recordTime`. Other documented kinds include `correction` and
`retraction`. Events are append-only in the interpreter; they do not
rewrite earlier rows.

A typical duty event:

```json
{
  "kind": "duty",
  "validTime": { "start": "NegInf", "end": "PosInf" },
  "recordTime": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "payload": {
    "kind": "ctor",
    "data": { "name": "Performed", "fields": {} }
  }
}
```

`validTime` is an interval (`start` / `end` are `NegInf`, `PosInf`,
`Inclusive` of an instant, or `Exclusive` of an instant). `recordTime`
is a single RFC 3339 instant.

## Annotated example: court selects I2

The fixture
[`examples/trust/cases/court-selects-i2.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/examples/trust/cases/court-selects-i2.json)
is a complete case for `Examples.BryanRevocableTrust`. The module
declares interpretation family `SuccessorEligibility` with alternatives
I1 (Alice and Bob both eligible) and I2 (only Bob eligible). Two
physician certificates and an occupancy record are on file. A court (or
other controlling selector) has already chosen I2.

```json
{
  "schema": "fidryn.case-record/v0.1",
  "module": "Examples.BryanRevocableTrust@0.1.0",
  "facts": {
    "alice_accepted": true,
    "bob_accepted": true
  },
  "evidence": [
    {
      "schema": "OccupancyRecord",
      "value": "Bryan",
      "observedAt": "2026-08-23T12:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "schema": "PhysicianCertificate",
      "value": "certificate-1",
      "observedAt": "2026-08-23T12:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "schema": "PhysicianCertificate",
      "value": "certificate-2",
      "observedAt": "2026-08-23T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "interpretations": {
    "SuccessorEligibility": "I2"
  },
  "admissibleCompletions": {
    "interpretations": {
      "SuccessorEligibility": ["I1", "I2"]
    }
  }
}
```

What each part is doing:

- `schema` identifies the interchange format. Reject anything else.
- `module` names the fixture this record is meant to accompany. Compile
  `examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr`; do not treat this string as
  a source-snapshot digest.
- `facts.alice_accepted` and `facts.bob_accepted` record that both
  nominees have accepted office. They are booleans, not propositions.
- `OccupancyRecord` with value `Bryan` is who occupies `TrusteeOf(BRT)`
  at the observation instant. Unique-occupant queries need this (or an
  equivalent ledger row). Two occupants for one office are
  `inconsistent`.
- Two `PhysicianCertificate` rows, both observed at
  `2026-08-23T12:00:00Z`, are the concurring record the instrument's
  incapacity judgment expects. If `--known-at` is earlier than that
  instant, neither certificate counts.
- `interpretations.SuccessorEligibility` is `I2`, which is a member of
  the declared domain `["I1", "I2"]`. That selection is already on the
  case, so `run` does not suspend for `needInterpretation`, and
  `explore` does not also try I1.
- `admissibleCompletions` is nonempty. The still-admissible worlds are
  exactly those two named alternatives, of which one has been chosen.
  Contrast
  [`two-certificates-open-eligibility.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/examples/trust/cases/two-certificates-open-eligibility.json),
  which has the same certificates and domain but no recorded
  interpretation: `run` stays suspended, `explore` is contingent between
  Alice and Bob.

Against `acting_trustee` with `--valid-at` / `--known-at` at or after
the observation times, both `run` and `explore` answer Bob. That
agreement is not a general guarantee; see [Outcomes](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md).

## Checklist

1. Set `"schema": "fidryn.case-record/v0.1"`.
2. Declare every still-open family, evidence schema, and choice protocol
   under `admissibleCompletions`. Leave a family off the object only if
   it is not part of this model.
3. Put recorded interpretations and decisions in those declared lists.
4. Timestamp evidence with `observedAt` and choose `--known-at` so that
   later records do not leak into an earlier file.
5. Tag decimals. Do not store amounts as bare strings.
6. Wrap user objects that need fields named `kind` and `data` as
   `{ "kind": "record", "data": { ... } }`.
7. Do not expect a `duty` event to perform an obligation unless an
   `AuthorityGrant` covers the action, or the event is an explicit
   `assumption`.
8. Treat `outsideScope` as part of the answer. The envelope will repeat
   it on `modelBoundary`.

========== https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md ==========

---
title: "Law modules"
description: "The reference of Fidryn law modules of edition 2: addresses, hashes, syntax, workspaces, references, definitions, bindings, change sets and the importer of the United States Code."
url: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules"
markdown: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md"
author: "Bryan Gass"
---

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules
> This markdown mirror is for agents and plain-text readers.

# Law modules

A law module is a file of edition 2. It holds provisions of law as data,
with their notes and what the source says of them, each named by an
address and covered by hashes; or, written by hand, it gives names to
provisions and binds names to them. Nothing in a law module is evaluated.
Law modules stand in workspaces: a generated workspace holds what an
importer writes from the archives of one release, and a curated workspace
holds modules written by hand, which may depend on generated workspaces.
`fidryn check` checks one module or a whole workspace, and `fidryn changes`
says what changed between two releases.

This reference gives, in this order: the two editions; the addresses of
modules, provisions and notes, and the file path of a module; the
normalization of text; the model of provisions, notes and layers; their
hashes; the syntax of edition 2, with three modules written in it; what the
checker verifies in one module; workspaces, their manifest and their lock,
and what the checker verifies in one; how a workspace is checked, and the
outcome of each reference; the cache of the check; the definitions that the
ingester extracts and the patterns it reads them by; curated modules, their
names, the dependencies of a curated workspace and its bindings; change
sets; the ingester for the United States Code, what it reads and what it
does not import; what is counted, in the coverage ledger and in the sample
of the Code that the repository holds; and the limits of all of these.

The crate `fidryn-provision` implements the model and the rules over it,
`fidryn-syntax` reads the text of a module, `fidryn-check` lowers it into
the model and checks it, `fidryn-driver` checks a workspace, writes a
generated one and compares two, and `fidryn-ingest-uscode` imports the
Code. In the examples, `/zz/demo` is an invented corpus.

## Editions

A `.fr` file is of one of two editions. A file of the first edition is a
program of the language that [Language](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/language.md) describes, and
carries no marker. A file of edition 2 is a law module: its first two
significant tokens are the word `edition` and the integer `2`; white
space, line ends and comments before them are skipped. A file whose first
significant token is anything else is a file of the first edition. A file
that begins with the word `edition` followed by anything other than `2` is
refused with `E100`: "unknown edition `3`; this toolchain reads edition 2
after the word `edition`, and files of the first edition carry no marker".

`fidryn_syntax::edition::edition_of` tells the edition of a file, and each
entry point asks it before it reads the file. The command line asks it of
a regular file only: an input that is no regular file, such as a pipe or
`/dev/stdin`, could not be read twice, and every command reads it as a
file of the first edition.

| Entry point | Given a module of edition 2 |
| --- | --- |
| `fidryn check FILE` | the checks of one module, as [below](#what-the-checker-verifies-in-one-module), then `ok` |
| `fidryn check DIR` | the checks of the workspace in the directory, every module of it included, as under [Workspaces](#workspaces) |
| `fmt`, `inputs`, `run`, `explore`, `explain`, `verify`, `diff`, `render`, `review` and `file` | exit 1 with `E100`: "an edition 2 module holds provisions and is not compiled for evaluation; `fidryn check` reads it" |
| `fidryn_cli::compile_source` and `compile_module`, and so the source pasted into the mill of `ui` | the same `E100` |
| the documentation check, `cargo xtask docs` | a fenced block, untagged or tagged `fidryn`, whose first line that is not blank is `edition 2` is a complete module and gets the checks of one module |

## Addresses

An address names a module, a provision or a note. It is `/` followed by one
or more segments separated by `/`:

```text
Address = "/" Segment { "/" Segment }
Segment = one or more of: ASCII letters, ASCII digits, "-", ".", "~" and the en dash U+2013
```

- A segment is never empty, never `.` and never `..`.
- Two addresses are equal when their texts are equal byte for byte:
  `/us/usc/t1/s8/a` and `/us/usc/t1/s8/A` are different addresses.
  Addresses are ordered by the bytes of their text.
- The full stop and the en dash occur in the identifiers of the United
  States Code: `s1395i–3`, `rule71.1`, `s44...46`. No identifier of the Code
  holds `~`. An ingester writes `~`, and only an ingester, to mark what it
  added to an identifier, as in `s1932~2`.
- The first segment names the authority that issues the names below it, the
  second the corpus. Nothing interprets either.
- The parent of an address is the address without its last segment. An
  address of one segment has no parent.
- An address is within another when it equals the other or lies below it at
  a segment boundary: `/us/usc/t1/s8/a` is within `/us/usc/t1/s8`, and
  `/us/usc/t1/s80` is not.

In JSON an address is a string that holds its text. A string that is no
address is refused when it is read.

`Address::parse` refuses a text that is no address and names the fault, with
the segment it lies in, counted from 0:

| Text | Refused because |
| --- | --- |
| the empty text | it is empty |
| `us/usc/t1` | it does not begin with `/` |
| `/us//t1` | segment 1 is empty |
| `/us/usc/` | segment 2 is empty |
| `/us/./t1`, `/us/../t1` | segment 1 is `.` or `..` |
| `/us/usc/t1 s8`, `/us/usc/t1_s8`, `/us/usc/t1%20s8` | segment 2 holds a space, `_` or `%` |

## File paths

A module with address `A` is the file `layout::module_path(A)` under its
workspace's root:

1. Each segment of the address maps to one path segment, character by
   character:

   | Character of the address | In the path |
   | --- | --- |
   | a lower-case ASCII letter, a digit or `~` | kept |
   | an upper-case ASCII letter | `_` followed by its lower-case form |
   | the en dash U+2013 | `-` |
   | the ASCII hyphen | `%2D` |
   | a full stop | kept, except as the first or the last character of a segment and before the letters `fr` that end a segment, where it is `%2E` |

2. If the mapped segment, or its part before its first full stop, compared
   without regard to case, is one of `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1` to
   `com9` or `lpt1` to `lpt9`, its first character is written as `%`
   followed by the two upper-case hexadecimal digits of its code.
3. The path is the mapped segments joined by `/`, followed by `.fr`. The
   separator is `/` on every host.

| Address | File path |
| --- | --- |
| `/us/usc/t29/s2611` | `us/usc/t29/s2611.fr` |
| `/us/usc/t42/s1395i–3` | `us/usc/t42/s1395i-3.fr` |
| `/us/usc/t2/s44...46` | `us/usc/t2/s44...46.fr` |
| `/us/usc/t5/ptIII/sptE` | `us/usc/t5/pt_i_i_i/spt_e.fr` |
| `/us/usc/t28a/courtRules/Civil/rule6` | `us/usc/t28a/court_rules/_civil/rule6.fr` |
| `/us/usc/t28/s1932~2` | `us/usc/t28/s1932~2.fr` |
| `/zz/demo/a-b` | `zz/demo/a%2Db.fr` |
| `/zz/demo/a.` | `zz/demo/a%2E.fr` |
| `/zz/demo/con` | `zz/demo/%63on.fr` |
| `/zz/demo/con.1` | `zz/demo/%63on.1.fr` |
| `/zz/demo/lpt1` | `zz/demo/%6Cpt1.fr` |
| `/zz/demo/.a` | `zz/demo/%2Ea.fr` |
| `/zz/demo/a.fr/b` | `zz/demo/a%2Efr/b.fr` |
| `/zz/demo/a..fr` | `zz/demo/a.%2Efr.fr` |

No path segment begins with a full stop, and none ends in a full stop or in
`.fr`, so the file of one module never has the name of another module's
directory: `/zz/demo/a.fr/b` is `zz/demo/a%2Efr/b.fr`, beside the file
`zz/demo/a.fr` of the address `/zz/demo/a`.

The mapping is one to one, so two addresses never share a path, also on a
file system that ignores case: `/zz/demo/ch6A` is `zz/demo/ch6_a.fr` and
`/zz/demo/ch6a` is `zz/demo/ch6a.fr`.

`layout::address_of_path` reads a path back as its address. It refuses
every path that the three rules do not write, such as `zz/demo/CH1.fr`,
`zz/demo/a_.fr`, `zz/demo/a%2d.fr`, `zz/demo/a%5F.fr`, `zz/demo/con.fr`,
`zz/demo/.a.fr`, `zz/demo/a.fr/b.fr`, `zz/demo/a.txt` and `zz\demo\a.fr`.
The path `zz/demo/a-b.fr` is the address `/zz/demo/a–b`, with an en dash.

## Normalization

The text of a law module is normalized. `normalize::normalize` normalizes a
text in four steps:

1. Put the text into Unicode Normalization Form C.
2. Replace each of the 25 characters with the Unicode property `White_Space`
   with U+0020: U+0009 to U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to
   U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000.
3. Replace each run of U+0020 with one.
4. Remove U+0020 at the start and at the end.

Nothing else changes: no case folding, and no change to quotation marks or
dashes. U+200B (zero width space) and U+FEFF are not white space and are
kept. `normalize::is_normalized` tells whether a text is normalized, that
is, whether normalizing it leaves it unchanged.

| Text | Normalized |
| --- | --- |
| two spaces, `a`, two spaces, `b`, one space | `a b` |
| `a`, U+00A0, `b` | `a b` |
| `§`, U+202F, `1` | `§ 1` |
| `Current`, U+2000, `through` | `Current through` |
| `a`, tab, `b`, line feed, `c`, carriage return, line feed, `d` | `a b c d` |
| `e`, U+0301 | `é` (U+00E9) |
| `1`, U+00A0, `000` | `1 000` |
| U+3000, `a`, U+1680 | `a` |
| `a`, U+200B, `b` | unchanged |
| U+FEFF, `a` | unchanged |
| `[sic]` | unchanged |
| `“x” — y` | unchanged |

The unit of normalization is the block: a paragraph, a heading, a number or
a paragraph of a table cell. The text of a block is the words of its runs,
concatenated, and that text is normalized: a run may begin or end with a
space, a block may not.

## Provisions, notes and layers

A module of law has one of three shapes:

- A **unit** holds one tree of provisions, whose top provision has the
  module's address. It also records the other addresses the source gives
  it (`aliases`), the container it stands in (`within`), the member of the
  source archive it was read from (`source`) and whether the source marks it
  as positive law (`positive_law`, which may be unknown), and it holds a
  source credit, notes, footnotes and definitions.
- A **container**, such as a chapter, has a kind, a number, a heading and a
  status of its own and lists its members: the containers and units directly
  below it, in document order. It holds a source credit, notes and
  footnotes, and records `aliases`, `within`, `source` and `positive_law` as
  a unit does.
- A **curated** module is written by hand. It imports modules, names
  addresses (citations) and binds names to provisions (bindings). A binding
  records the release it was made against and two hashes, one of the
  provision and one of the enacted notes of its unit, which tell when it
  is [stale](#bindings).

The crate holds the model in its module `model`.

### Provisions

A provision has an address, a kind, a number, a heading and a status, each
