is loaded. A saved v0.2 report from `run` / `explore` retains the actual
parented derivation in `traceDocument`; `explain` uses those nodes. Legacy
outcome-only documents have only the provenance their compatibility projection
retained. If no such file exists, the argument is hashed as a
`TraceId` and the node list is empty. JSON always includes a `nodes`
array; emptiness means no persisted DAG was loaded, not an omitted field.
Unknown `--format` values are treated as `text`.

**Example**

```text
fidryn run examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr \
  --query acting_trustee \
  --case examples/trust/cases/one-certificate.json \
  --valid-at 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z \
  --known-at 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z \
  > outcome.json

fidryn explain outcome.json --format text
```

The first command writes `outcome.json` in the working directory.

Without a file, the id is hashed and the DAG is empty:

```sh
fidryn explain 00000000000000000000000000000000 --format json
```

**Success.** Formatted trace on stdout. Text with no nodes is
`trace <hex>`. JSON is a canonical `TraceDocument`. DOT is a `digraph`.

**Failure.** Exit 1. `cannot read PATH: ...` or `invalid trace JSON PATH: ...`.

## `verify`

Check a property of a module. A `verify` block declares one under its
name. A `for_all` or an `exists` written in a query, in a `verify` block
or as a declaration of its own is a property as well. It is named after
its kind, its variable and its number among the quantifiers written in
those places, counted from 0 in the order of the text: `for_all:x:0`.
Such a property has no bounds, and its verdict is `unknown`. Query names
are not properties.

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PATH` | yes | path to a `.fr` file |
| `--property NAME` | yes | property name |

**Example**

```sh exit=1
fidryn verify examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr --property TrusteeContinuity
```

`TrusteeContinuity` is declared on that module. A bounded check that does
not obtain a covering proof is not success: the CLI prints the verdict to
stderr and exits 1. Only a proved verdict is exit 0. The bounded supported
fragment includes structured Boolean/arithmetic assertions and finite quantified
formulas; every assertion in the named block must hold.
[The fields of a verify block](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/language.md#the-fields-of-a-verify-block)
says which parts of a block are its assertions. Unsupported formulas, a
block with no assertion and resource exhaustion remain `unknown`. Passing a
query name such as `acting_trustee` is invalid.

**Success.** Stdout, for example
`proved NAME (persons=..., events=..., time_points=...)`.

**Failure.** Exit 1, stderr. Check diagnostics, or a verdict such as
`unknown NAME: ...`, `counterexample for NAME: ...`,
`` `NAME` is a query, not a declared verification property ``, or
`unknown property NAME`.

## `diff`

Compare two snapshots and print canonical JSON with two named
operations: `result` (outcomeDocument / compiled query bodies) and
`assurance` (executionMode, sourceTrust, assumptions,
verificationMethod, coverage, invocation/source/executable identity and
exploration evidence). Each is `{added, removed, changed}`. Changing only
qualifications is an assurance diff, not a silent equal. A `.fr` path is
compiled; any other path is read as JSON (an evaluation report, mill
`{ok, report}` wrapper, outcome document, or serialized module).

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OLD_SNAPSHOT` | yes | `.fr` path or JSON file |
| `NEW_SNAPSHOT` | yes | `.fr` path or JSON file |
| `--query NAME` | yes | query name used when JSON has no embedded names |

**Example**

```sh
fidryn diff \
  examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr \
  examples/california/final-pay/final-pay.fr \
  --query acting_trustee
```

Identical snapshots (the same file twice) print empty arrays under both
`result` and `assurance`.

**Success.** One canonical JSON object on stdout:

```
{"assurance":{"added":[],"changed":[],"removed":[]},"result":{"added":[],"changed":[],"removed":[]}}
```

Each of `result` and `assurance` has keys `added`, `removed`, and
`changed` (sorted arrays of strings).

**Failure.** Exit 1. Compile diagnostics for `.fr` inputs;
`cannot read PATH`; `invalid snapshot JSON PATH: ...`; or
`cannot encode diff: ...`.

## `render`

Interpolate Core fields into a template. Available keys from the compiled
module are `module`, `version`, typed `outside_scope` and its text
`outside_scope_label`. Optional `--data DATA.json` adds typed values under `data`.
`{{#each data.people}}{{name}}{{/each}}` iterates records without splitting names
on punctuation. Missing keys fail
closed. A directory named `certified` does not approve legal content;
`templates/certified/` files are interpolation fixtures only.

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PATH` | yes | path to a `.fr` file |
| `--template TEMPLATE` | yes | path to a template file |
| `--data DATA.json` | no | typed JSON under the `data` template key |

**Example**

```sh
fidryn render examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr \
  --template templates/certified/instrument-outline.txt
```

**Success.** Rendered text on stdout (no extra newline beyond the
template).

**Failure.** Exit 1. Check diagnostics; `cannot read TEMPLATE`; or
`missing template key \`...\``.

## `file`

Submit a JSON filing packet through an adapter. Dry-run is the default.
Live HTTP requires both `--live` and the environment variable
`FIDRYN_ALLOW_LIVE_FILING=1`. A successful transport receipt is not a
`Filed` legal fact.

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PACKET.json` | yes | JSON file holding one Fidryn value in tagged form (see below) |
| `--adapter NAME` | no | `dry-run` (default), `ma-corporations`, or `massachusetts` |
| `--live` | no | flag; enable live HTTP when the adapter and env allow it |
| `--endpoint URL` | no | live POST URL for the Massachusetts adapter |

`--adapter massachusetts` is an alias of `ma-corporations`. Any other
adapter name uses dry-run. The dry-run adapter refuses `--live` even if
the environment variable is set. The Massachusetts adapter’s default
endpoint is `https://www.sec.state.ma.us/filing`.

A packet is one Fidryn value in its tagged JSON form: an object whose
`kind` names the kind of value, such as `string`, `int`, `bool` or `map`,
and whose `data` holds it, as in `{"kind":"string","data":"x"}`. A `map`
holds named values in the same form. Other JSON, a case record included,
is refused with `invalid packet JSON` and exit 1.
[`tests/programs/packets/dry-run.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/tests/programs/packets/dry-run.json)
is a small packet: a `map` of two strings.

Without `--live`, every adapter answers as the dry-run adapter does: it
prints the packet back as `{"kind":"dryRun","packet":...}`, makes no
network request and writes no file.

```sh
fidryn file tests/programs/packets/dry-run.json
```

Live shape (does not establish `Filed`):

```text
FIDRYN_ALLOW_LIVE_FILING=1 fidryn file \
  tests/programs/packets/dry-run.json \
  --adapter ma-corporations \
  --live \
  --endpoint https://www.sec.state.ma.us/filing
```

**Success.** Adapter JSON on stdout (`kind` is camelCase): `dryRun` with
the packet echoed; or, for live Massachusetts HTTP, `accepted` (with
`filingId` and `raw`), `rejected`, `transportFailure`, or
`submissionUncertain`. `accepted` is a transport receipt.

**Failure.** Exit 1. `cannot read PACKET`; `invalid packet JSON`; or
`live filing is disabled (set FIDRYN_ALLOW_LIVE_FILING=1 and pass --live)`.

The [mill](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md) has no filing route.

## `ui`

Serve the localhost mill. See [mill](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md) for routes and the HTML
page. The process binds `127.0.0.1` only and does not live-file.

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--port N` | no | `u16` TCP port on loopback (default 8751) |
| `--no-open` | no | flag; do not attempt to open a browser |

This build does not link an opener crate. Without `--no-open`, stderr
notes that browser auto-open is not linked. With `--no-open`, that line
is omitted.

**Example**

```sh
fidryn ui --port 8751 --no-open
```

**Success.** The server runs until Ctrl-C. Stderr includes
`fidryn mill on http://127.0.0.1:PORT` and
`127.0.0.1 only. live filing is disabled.` Exit 0 after shutdown.

**Failure.** Exit 1.
`127.0.0.1:PORT is already in use. Stop that process or pass --port.`
Other bind or runtime errors are printed to stderr.

## `inputs`

`fidryn inputs MODULE --query QUERY` emits JSON Schema for the declared query
argument object. Aliases, sum constructors, records, nominal entities and
collections come from checked declarations. Observation schemas and external
review requests appear as metadata. Unsupported representations refuse instead
of producing an unconstrained input schema.

## `review`

`fidryn review MODULE --query QUERY --case CASE.json --valid-at TIME --known-at
TIME` emits a portable `fidryn.review-bundle/v0.1` JSON archive. It retains exact
source/case/dependency/lock bytes, a labeled normalized manifest, checked report
and actual trace, source spans, executable digest and rerun arguments. Optional
`--scenario`, `--budget N` and `--template FILE` select the disclosed evaluation
or retain reviewer material. Reviewer status is `not_assessed`; the archive does
not constitute legal approval. See [Development and promotion](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/development.md).

## `ingest`

`fidryn ingest uscode ARCHIVE_DIR --out DIR` imports the United States
Code from the archives of one release of the official XML release point
published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel, each verified against
the retrieval record beside them, and writes a generated workspace that
`fidryn check DIR` accepts
([The ingester for the United States Code](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#the-ingester-for-the-united-states-code)).
The same archives, the same titles and the same version of the toolchain
give the same bytes on every run and on every host, for any number of
workers.

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ARCHIVE_DIR` | yes | path to the directory of the archives of one release and their retrieval record, `retrieval.json` |
| `--out DIR` | yes | path to the directory of the workspace: one that does not exist, one that holds nothing but entries whose name begins with a dot, or an earlier output of the command |
| `--title T` | no | a title to write, by the publisher's designation, such as `1` or `5a`, its letter in either case; may be given more than once; by default every title of the release |
| `--jobs N` | no | the number of worker threads, at least 1; by default as many as the system reports as available |
| `--verify` | no | flag; write nothing, and report every entry under `DIR` that differs from what the run would write |

A run writes `workspace.json` first, then each module, each file through
a temporary file that is renamed; it removes the modules of an earlier
output that it does not write, and writes `law.lock.json` and then, last,
`coverage.json`, the [coverage ledger](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#the-coverage-ledger)
of the workspace, which [`coverage`](#coverage) prints; so a run that is
stopped leaves a directory the next run accepts. The lock does not list
the ledger. With `--title`,
only the modules of those titles are written, and the lock lists the
archives and members whose modules the run wrote. The numbering of
addresses still runs over every member the archive directory holds,
whichever titles are chosen, so an address does not depend on the
selection.

An earlier output of the command is a generated workspace of the prefix
`/us/usc` whose `.fr` files are each a module of edition 2 whose address
lies below the prefix and which stands at the path of its address. A run
reads the head of every `.fr` file of `DIR`, its marker and the address
after `module`, in its first 64 KiB, before it writes anything, and
removes only such modules.

`--verify` compares `workspace.json`, `law.lock.json`, `coverage.json`
and every module file of `DIR` with what the run would write. Every other
entry that a run would refuse is extra: a file other than a module and
those three at the top, a symbolic link or any other entry that is
neither a file nor a directory, and a `.fr` file that is no earlier output,
which is different instead where the run writes a module. Only the entries
whose name begins with a dot are not looked at. It writes nothing, `DIR`
included. A run stopped after the lock and before the ledger leaves a
workspace that `fidryn check` accepts, since no check reads the ledger,
and `--verify` reports it as
`missing coverage.json`, or `different coverage.json` when the ledger is
that of an earlier run.

**Example**

```text
fidryn ingest uscode samples/uscode/archives --out DIR
fidryn ingest uscode samples/uscode/archives --out DIR --title 1 --jobs 4
fidryn check DIR
fidryn ingest uscode samples/uscode/archives --out DIR --verify
```

**Success.** Prints one line and exits 0:

```text
ingested: U units, C containers from A archives (release R)
```

A noun whose count is 1 is in the singular, as in
`ingested: 1 unit, 1 container from 1 archive (release R)`.

With `--verify`, prints `ok` when nothing differs: `DIR` then holds every
file the run would write, with the same bytes, and nothing a run would
refuse, so a run into it is accepted and changes none of its bytes.

**Failure.** Exit 1. A release that is refused, by its retrieval record or
by a reading rule, is reported with the archive, the member and, for a
document, the element, the line it starts on and the nearest identifier.
A title that no member holds is reported, by the designation given,
before anything is written. A directory that holds anything other than an
earlier output of the command is refused with what it holds, and nothing
in it is changed: every `.fr` file that is no earlier output is named, a
file of the first edition, a module of another prefix and a module at
another path among them. With `--verify`, each path under `DIR` that differs is
printed to stdout, relative to `DIR`, in the byte order of the paths,
after the word that says how: `missing`, `extra` or `different`. The exit
status is 1:

```text
extra notes.txt
extra us/usc/link
different us/usc/t99/s1.fr
extra us/usc/t99/s7.fr
missing us/usc/t99a.fr
```

## `text`

`fidryn text DIR` prints the text of the provisions and notes of the
workspace in `DIR`: of every provision, container, note, source credit and
footnote of its modules, read from its module files
([Workspaces](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#workspaces)). With `ADDRESS` it prints the
provision, container or note at that address and what lies below it: every
one whose address is `ADDRESS` or continues it at a segment boundary. With
`ADDRESS` and `--hashes` it prints the two hashes that a binding to that
provision records instead ([Bindings](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#bindings)). It reads
the modules and checks nothing else of the workspace, which
`fidryn check DIR` does.

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DIR` | yes | path to the directory of a workspace |
| `ADDRESS` | no | the address of a provision, a container or a note of the workspace; with `--hashes`, of a provision, or an alias of a unit |
| `--json` | no | flag; print one text record to a line |
| `--hashes` | no | flag; print the two lines that a binding to `ADDRESS` records; needs `ADDRESS`, and is not given with `--json` |

**Example**

```sh
fidryn text conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo
fidryn text conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo /zz/demo/t1/s2
fidryn text conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo --json
fidryn text conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo /zz/demo/t1/s2 --hashes
fidryn text samples/uscode/workspace /us/usc/t1/s1
```

**Success.** Exit 0. Without `--json` it prints the text for a person,
module by module in the order of their addresses, with a blank line
between two modules:

- A provision is its address on a line of its own, followed by its status
  in parentheses when it has one; then its number and heading on one line,
  the blocks of its text parts and its children, each indented by two
  spaces for each level of depth. The provision printed first is at depth
  0.
- A table is one line for each row, its cells separated by ` | `. The items
  of quoted content are indented one level further. A footnote marker is
  its shown text in brackets, and an image is `[image SOURCE]`.
- After the provisions of a unit come its source credit and its footnotes,
  each footnote after its marker in brackets, and then its notes, each its
  address with its layer in parentheses, its heading and its blocks. A
  container is its address, its number and heading, its credit, its
  footnotes and its notes.

Of the demo workspace, `fidryn text conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo /zz/demo/t1`
prints:

```text
/zz/demo/t1
  Title 1— Invented Things

/zz/demo/t1/ch1
  Chapter 1— Widgets

/zz/demo/t1/s1
  § 1. Definitions
  In this invented chapter, a widget is a small device.

/zz/demo/t1/s2
  § 2. Sizes
  A widget is small or large.

/zz/demo/t1/s3
  § 3. Colors
  A widget may be of any color.
```

With `--json` it prints one text record, `fidryn.text-record/v0.1`, to a
line, the JSON Schema of which is
[schemas/text-record-v0.1.json](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/text-record-v0.1.json). The
records are those of every module, sorted by the bytes of their addresses
across the whole workspace; for one address the provision or container
comes first, then the source credit, then the footnotes by ordinal. Each
is one line of compact JSON with its keys in this order:

| Record | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| a provision | `address`, `layer` (`"operative"`), `kind`, `status` (the word, or `null`), `num`, `heading`, `items`, where an item is a text part `{"part": role, "blocks": [...]}` or a child `{"child": address}`; the top provision of a unit also `aliases`, `within`, `source` and `positive_law` |
| a container | `address`, `layer` (`"operative"`), `kind`, `status`, `num`, `heading`, `aliases`, `within`, `members` |
| a note | `address`, `layer` (`"enacted"` or `"editorial"`), `group`, `topics`, `heading`, `blocks` |
| a source credit | the address of its module, `record` (`"credit"`), and the keys of a paragraph |
| a footnote | the address of its module, `record` (`"footnote"`), `ordinal`, `shown`, `blocks` |

A text is `{"text": plain, "refs": [[start, end, target], ...], "sup":
[[start, end], ...], "sub": [[start, end], ...]}`, followed by `"marks":
[[offset, shown, footnote], ...]` when it holds a footnote marker. Offsets
count the Unicode scalar values of the plain text, an end is exclusive, and
the offset of a marker is the length of the plain text before it. A
paragraph is a text with the key `p` in place of `text`, a subheading one
with the key `subheading`. A heading is `null` or a text, and a number is
`null` or `[value, shown]`, `shown` the plain string when it is words only
and a text otherwise. A table is `{"table": [[group, [[header, colspan,
rowspan, [blocks]], ...]], ...]}`, an image `{"image": source}`, and
quoted content `{"quoted": {"origin": origin, "items": [...]}}`, whose
items are blocks, text parts and levels `{"level": kind, "num": ...,
"heading": ..., "items": [...]}`. The record of `/zz/demo/t1/s2`:

```text
{"address":"/zz/demo/t1/s2","layer":"operative","kind":"section","status":null,"num":["2","§ 2."],"heading":{"text":"Sizes","refs":[],"sup":[],"sub":[]},"items":[{"part":"content","blocks":[{"p":"A widget is small or large.","refs":[],"sup":[],"sub":[]}]}],"aliases":[],"within":"/zz/demo/t1/ch1","source":"demo01.xml","positive_law":true}
```

Both forms depend on the module files alone: neither the host, the
working directory nor the number of threads the system offers changes a
byte. `conformance/uslm_text.py` prints the same records from the
publisher's XML, independently of the ingester, and the check of the
sample of the Code compares the two line for line
([The sample](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#the-sample)).

With `--hashes` it prints exactly two lines and nothing else, the two
that a person writes into a binding after its `release`: the tree hash of
the provision at `ADDRESS`, or of the top provision of the unit that
`ADDRESS` is an alias of, and the hash of the enacted layer of that unit,
each as 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits. They come from the
[interfaces](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#interfaces) of the modules, the place the check
of a workspace takes them from, so a binding that records them is not
stale against the workspace they were printed from. Of the demo
workspace, `fidryn text conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo /zz/demo/t1/s2 --hashes`
prints:

```text
provision_hash "238c20bcd64758ed0b7f1e2eed5758d78ff4abda212539e8b9e7a07b7301686f"
notes_hash "a396bac23ba81b30cb34dbf808cf06deeaeb4b87e010b66646faadc6accfc6ff"
```

**Failure.** Exit 1. Nothing is printed to stdout, and the reason is
printed to stderr: a directory that holds no workspace (`E730`), an entry
that cannot be read or is neither a file nor a directory (`E730`), a
module file that is not a module of edition 2 that lowers, each with its
diagnostics; a text that is no address; and an address at which the
workspace holds no provision, container or note, as
``the workspace holds no provision, container or note at `/zz/demo/t1/s9` ``:

```sh exit=1
fidryn text conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo /zz/demo/t1/s9
```

With `--hashes`, an address that is no provision and no alias of a unit is
refused in the same way, saying what it is: the address of a note, of a
container or of a curated module, an alias of a container, or the address
of nothing, as
``the workspace holds no provision, container or note at `/zz/demo/t1/s9` ``.
The chapter of the demo workspace is a container:

```sh exit=1
fidryn text conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo /zz/demo/t1/ch1 --hashes
```

`--hashes` without `ADDRESS`, and `--hashes` with `--json`, are usage
errors, exit 2.

## `coverage`

`fidryn coverage DIR` prints the coverage ledger of the generated workspace
in `DIR`, `fidryn.coverage/v0.1`: its units, containers and provisions,
its notes, footnotes and images, its references of each layer by outcome,
the definitions extracted from its provisions by basis and by kind, and
what its importer counted and did not import
([The coverage ledger](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#the-coverage-ledger)). It computes the
ledger from the modules as their files stand, the manifest and the lock.
It does not verify the module files against the lock, which is what
`fidryn check DIR` is for. Of a workspace whose files are those its run
wrote, it prints that run's `coverage.json`, byte for byte.

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DIR` | yes | path to the directory of a generated workspace |

**Example**

```sh
fidryn coverage conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo
fidryn coverage samples/uscode/workspace
```

**Success.** Exit 0. It prints the ledger as JSON with two spaces of
indentation and a final line end, its keys in their order, the JSON Schema
of which is [schemas/coverage-v0.1.json](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/coverage-v0.1.json).
Of the demo workspace it prints first:

```text
{
  "schema": "fidryn.coverage/v0.1",
  "prefix": "/zz/demo",
  "release": "42-7",
  "totals": {
    "units": 3,
    "containers": 2,
    "provisions": 3,
    "units_by_kind": {
      "section": 3
    },
```

The output depends on the files of the workspace alone: neither the host,
the working directory nor the number of threads the system offers changes
a byte. The figures of the sample of the Code are on the page
[Coverage](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/coverage.md).

**Failure.** Exit 1. Nothing is printed to stdout, and the reason is
printed to stderr: a curated workspace, which has no ledger, as
``DIR holds a curated workspace, and the coverage ledger belongs to a generated workspace, whose lock records what its importer counted``;
a directory that holds no workspace (`E730`); a generated workspace
without a lock, with one that cannot be read, or with one whose prefix or
release is not the manifest's (`E730`); an entry that cannot be read or is
neither a file nor a directory (`E730`); and a module file that is not a
module of edition 2 that lowers, with its diagnostics. The curated sample
of the repository is refused:

```sh exit=1
fidryn coverage samples/uscode/curated
```

## `changes`

`fidryn changes OLD_DIR NEW_DIR` prints the change set between two
generated workspaces of one prefix, the imports of two releases of one
corpus: the provisions, notes and containers added, removed, moved or
amended, by layer ([Change sets](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#change-sets)). With
`--bindings DIR` it also lists the bindings of the curated workspace in
`DIR` that are stale against `NEW_DIR`, whatever release that workspace is
pinned to: it answers what would go stale if the pin moved there. Each
workspace is read as `fidryn check` reads it, through phase one and the
cache. Only the modules whose hashes differ are read again, and the units
on one side only whose top provision has the kind and the status of a
provision on the other side only, so that the two could be one moved
provision.

**Arguments**

| Name | Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OLD_DIR` | yes | path to the directory of the older generated workspace |
| `NEW_DIR` | yes | path to the directory of the newer generated workspace, of the prefix of `OLD_DIR` |
| `--bindings DIR` | no | path to the directory of a curated workspace whose bindings are judged against `NEW_DIR`; may be given more than once, and a directory given twice is read once |
| `--json` | no | flag; print the change set as JSON, `fidryn.change-set/v0.1` |
| `--jobs N` | no | the number of worker threads, at least 1; by default as many as the system reports as available |
| `--cache-dir DIR` | no | the directory of the cache of every workspace read; by default the one [`check`](#check) keeps, `FIDRYN_CACHE_DIR` or `fidryn` in the cache directory of the user |
| `--no-cache` | no | flag; keep no cache: check every module file, and write no entry |

The cache is chosen, from the same variables, as by [`check`](#check), and
every workspace the command reads, the two sides and each `--bindings`
directory, shares it; nothing is written into any of them unless the
cache is named inside one. A check trusts its cache, so a cache belongs
where only people one trusts can write. `--cache-dir` and `--no-cache` are
not given together.

**Example**

Each of these compares a workspace with itself, with `--no-cache`, so that
no cache is written; each prints a change set in which nothing changed:

```sh
fidryn changes conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo --no-cache
fidryn changes conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo --no-cache --json
fidryn changes samples/uscode/workspace samples/uscode/workspace --no-cache --bindings samples/uscode/curated
```

```text
fidryn changes OLD_DIR NEW_DIR --bindings CURATED_DIR > message.txt
fidryn changes OLD_DIR NEW_DIR --json --jobs 8 > changes.json
```

**Success.** Exit 0. Without `--json` it prints the change set as the text
of a commit message: a first line `<prefix>: <old release> to <new release>`,
a blank line, one line of counts for each of the four groups, and then
each list that is not empty under its name, one entry to a line. Of the
demo workspace compared with itself:

```text
/zz/demo: 42-7 to 42-7

operative: 0 added, 0 removed, 0 amended_text, 0 amended_structure, 0 moved
enacted_notes: 0 added, 0 removed, 0 amended, 0 moved
editorial: 0 added, 0 removed, 0 amended, 0 moved, 0 credits_changed, 0 footnotes_changed
containers: 0 added, 0 removed, 0 changed
```

With `--json` it prints the change set as pretty JSON, every key present,
the JSON Schema of which is
[schemas/change-set-v0.1.json](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/change-set-v0.1.json). Every list
is sorted, and both forms are the same bytes on every run and for every
number of workers. [Change sets](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#change-sets) says what puts
an address into each list and shows the text of one.

When the cache of a workspace could not be used or could not be written,
the command says so once on stderr, as [`check`](#check) does, with
`the cache could not be used, and the check went on without it: ...` or
`the cache could not be written, and the check went on without it: ...`,
and the change set is what it would have been.

**Failure.** Exit 1, with nothing on stdout. A directory that holds no
workspace, a curated workspace as `OLD_DIR` or `NEW_DIR`, a generated one
as `--bindings`, and two workspaces of different prefixes are each refused
with one `E730` that says which, as
``this is the manifest of a curated workspace, and a change set is made between two generated workspaces``.
`conformance/fixtures/workspace` holds no `workspace.json`, and is refused
as no workspace:

```sh exit=1
fidryn changes conformance/fixtures/workspace conformance/fixtures/workspace/demo --no-cache
```

A workspace that has an error ends the command with its diagnostics, each
naming its file under the directory given, as `fidryn check` prints them;
for a curated workspace of `--bindings` these are the diagnostics of its
module files by themselves. When the command keeps no cache because no
directory is named for one, or because the identity of the running
executable cannot be read, it says so after the diagnostics of a failure
too, as `the cache could not be used, and the check went on without it: ...`;
what the checks of the workspaces it read found of their cache is said
only when the comparison succeeds.

## See also

- [Getting started](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started.md)
- [Mill](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md)

========== https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md ==========

---
title: "Mill"
description: "Localhost Fidryn mill UI on 127.0.0.1 — checks modules; does not live-file."
url: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill"
markdown: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md"
author: "Bryan Gass"
---

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill
> This markdown mirror is for agents and plain-text readers.

# Fidryn mill

The mill is a loopback-only web UI for checking, running, exploring, and
rendering Fidryn source on this machine. Start it with the CLI:

```text
fidryn ui [--port N] [--no-open]
```

Default port is 8751. The process listens on `127.0.0.1` only. It never
binds `0.0.0.0` or other interfaces. There is no filing route. Live
filing is not available from the mill.

See [getting started](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started.md) for a first module, and the
[CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md) for path-based `check` / `run` / `explore` / `render` /
`file`.

## Start

From a clone:

```sh
cargo run -p fidryn-cli -- ui --no-open
```

Or, after `cargo install --path crates/fidryn-cli`:

```sh
fidryn ui --port 8751 --no-open
```

On success, stderr prints:

```text
fidryn mill on http://127.0.0.1:8751
127.0.0.1 only. live filing is disabled.
```

Without `--no-open`, a further line says browser auto-open is not linked
and you should open the URL locally. This build does not launch a
browser. Ctrl-C shuts the server down. If the port is taken, the process
exits 1 with
`127.0.0.1:PORT is already in use. Stop that process or pass --port.`

## Routes

| Method | Path | Body | Success |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/` | none | `web/index.html` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), with the security headers below |
| `GET` | `/assets/fidryn.css` | none | `site/assets/fidryn.css`, the design system the site also uses (`text/css; charset=utf-8`) |
| `GET` | `/assets/mill.css` | none | `web/mill.css`, the mill's own styles (`text/css; charset=utf-8`) |
| `GET` | `/assets/mill.js` | none | `web/mill.js`, the mill app (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) |
| `GET` | `/favicon.svg` | none | `site/favicon.svg` (`image/svg+xml`) |
| `GET` | `/fonts/{name}` | none | `fraunces.woff2`, `plex-sans.woff2`, `plex-mono-400.woff2`, or `plex-mono-500.woff2` from `site/fonts/` (`font/woff2`); any other name is 404 |
| `GET` | `/api/health` | none | plain text `ok` |
| `GET` | `/api/samples` | none | JSON array of the built-in samples, each `{id, title, blurb, source, case, query, validAt, knownAt, action, expect}` |
| `POST` | `/api/check` | JSON `CheckRequest` | JSON `{ok, diagnostics}` |
| `POST` | `/api/run` | JSON `EvalRequest` | `{ "ok": true, "report": <evaluation-report>, "opinion": [<sentence>, ...] }` |
| `POST` | `/api/explore` | JSON `EvalRequest` | same transport as `/api/run` |
| `POST` | `/api/render` | JSON `RenderRequest` | JSON `{ok, text?, error?}` |

The page, its two stylesheets and script, the favicon, the fonts, and
the samples are compiled into the `fidryn` binary; the mill reads no
files at runtime. The page, stylesheets, script, favicon, and fonts are
sent with `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
`GET /` also sends
`Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`,
`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`,
so the browser runs no inline script or style on the page and will not
show it inside a frame. In a sample, `source` is the text of a
repository fixture and `case` is the text of a case file, or the empty
case record for the first two samples (`case` is JSON text, not a
parsed object); `expect` is the outcome kind that `action` returns
for it.

There is no `POST /api/file`, `/api/filing`, `/api/submit`, or
`/api/live`. Those paths return 404.

## JSON field names

Names below are the serde fields the mill actually reads. `EvalRequest`
uses camelCase. `CheckRequest` and `RenderRequest` do not.

### `POST /api/check`

```
{"source": "<fidryn module text>"}
```

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | string | yes |

HTTP status is 200 in both cases. Success is `{"ok": true, "diagnostics": []}`.
A failed check is `{"ok": false, "diagnostics": [...]}`. Each diagnostic
object has `code`, `message`, `primary_span`, `related_spans`, and
`suggestion` (Rust field names, snake_case).

### `POST /api/run` and `POST /api/explore`

```
{
  "source": "<fidryn module text>",
  "query": "q",
  "case": {},
  "bounds": null,
  "validAt": "2033-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "knownAt": "2033-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | string | yes |
| `query` | string | yes |
| `case` | JSON value | no (omitted, `{}`, or `null` is an empty case) |
| `bounds` | JSON value or omitted | no; used only by `/api/explore` |
| `validAt` | RFC 3339 string | yes |
| `knownAt` | RFC 3339 string | yes |

`case` must be a `fidryn.case-record/v0.1` object, `{}`, or JSON null.
`bounds` follows the same merge rules as CLI `--bounds`: an
`AdmissibleCompletions` object (`interpretations`, `evidence`, `choices`)
or a wrapper with `admissibleCompletions` / `admissible_completions`.
`/api/run` ignores `bounds`. `/api/explore` still needs a nonempty
completion space on the case, on `bounds`, or both; otherwise the
outcome is an empty completion set.

A nonempty `case.assumptions` array puts mill `/api/run` and
`/api/explore` into scenario mode (`executionMode: scenario` on the
report). There is no separate mill `--scenario` flag; the overlay is
inferred from the case. An empty or omitted `assumptions` list is
operative. CLI path `run` still requires explicit `--scenario` to apply
the same overlay.

`validAt` and `knownAt` accept a `Z` suffix or a numeric offset, the same
as CLI `--valid-at` and `--known-at`.

On evaluation success, HTTP 200, and the body is a transport wrapper
`{ "ok": true, "report": ..., "opinion": [...] }`
(`schemas/mill-evaluation-response-v0.1.json`). `report` is the
`fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2` envelope the CLI prints
(`schema`, `executionMode`, `assumptions`, `sourceTrust`,
`verificationMethod`, `coverage`, checked invocation and source/executable
identities, retained actual `traceDocument`, `outcomeDocument`, and exploration
`searchEvidence` when applicable). `opinion` is the
report read as plain sentences, for example
`acting_trustee depends on SuccessorEligibility.` and
`Under I1 it is Alice.` for a contingent trust run. Each sentence is a
fixed template filled from report fields, so it never says more than
the report does. `ok` and `opinion` are not fields of that report schema
(`additionalProperties` is false). Nested `outcomeDocument` is the
`fidryn.outcome/v0.1` projection. Pasted compile is
`sourceTrust: unauthenticated`. `run` never chooses a completion.

On check failure, HTTP 400:

```
{"ok": false, "error": "check failed", "diagnostics": [...]}
```

Invalid case, bounds, or timestamps are HTTP 400 with `ok` false, an
`error` string (`invalid case: ...`, the bounds merge message, or
`validAt:` / `knownAt:` plus the parse error), and `diagnostics: []`.

Unknown queries and other engine failures are HTTP 400 (HTTP 500 only
when the engine kind is `Internal`):

```
{"kind": "engineError", "error": "UnknownQuery", "message": "...", "ok": false}
```

`error` here is the engine kind (`UnknownQuery`, `Unsupported`,
`FuelExhausted`, `InvalidInput`, `Internal`), not a legal outcome kind.
It is not rewritten as `inconsistent`.

### `POST /api/render`

```
{"source": "<fidryn module text>", "template": "{{module}}@{{version}}"}
```

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |

HTTP status is 200 in both cases. Success is `{"ok": true, "text": "..."}`.
Failure (check diagnostics joined by newlines, or a missing template key)
is `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`. Template variables are `module`,
`version`, typed `outside_scope`, and `outside_scope_label`. An optional JSON
`data` field is available under the template key `data`; typed arrays and record
fields are preserved. Missing keys and collection type mismatches fail closed.

## In-memory compile versus path compile

Mill `source` is compiled with `compile_source` against
`SourceManifest::default()`. A `source_manifest` header in the pasted
text is not loaded. No artifact files are read. Hex import digests are
not byte-authenticated. No `.fr` or manifest is written to disk.

CLI `fidryn check PATH` (and `run` / `explore` / `verify` / `render` on a
path) uses `Driver::check_path`. That authenticates hex import digests
against files in the module directory. The digest `"fixture"` remains a
test trust profile, not that byte check. Details are in [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md)
under source checking and trust.

CLI path compile loads the declared manifest and, for hex digests, hashes
files next to the module. Mill pasted source does neither. A module that
`fidryn check` accepts can fail in the mill if its imports require a
digest the empty default manifest does not supply. Mill check of a
snippet never proves that on-disk artifacts are intact. Mill must not
gain filesystem access from paste.

## No live filing

The mill does not call filing adapters. `fidryn file` on the [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md)
is the only submit path, and even there live HTTP needs `--live` and
`FIDRYN_ALLOW_LIVE_FILING=1`. A transport receipt is still not `Filed`.
The HTML page states that live filing is not available from the UI.

## The HTML page

`GET /` serves `web/index.html`, which loads `/assets/fidryn.css` (the
site's design system), `/assets/mill.css`, and `/assets/mill.js`. Those
files, the fonts, and the samples are compiled into the binary, and the
page sends requests only to 127.0.0.1. The response carries a strict
Content-Security-Policy, so the page runs no inline script.

On screens 1200px and wider the page has three columns (samples and
history, the editor, and the query with the result); narrower screens
stack them in one column. From the top:

1. **Header.** The Fidryn monogram, `mill`, the health status
   (`localhost 127.0.0.1 · ok`, or a warning when the server cannot be
   reached), the notice "Live filing is not available from the UI", a
   link to this guide, and the theme toggle. The theme follows the
   system until you choose light or dark.
2. **Samples and history.** Samples come from `GET /api/samples`, each
   with the outcome kind its default action produces: `require-gate`,
   `late-payment`, and three runs of the trust fixture (open
   eligibility, court selects I2, one certificate). Choosing a sample
   fills the module, case, query, and both clocks, then runs its
   default action; if you have unsaved edits, the rail asks before
   replacing them. The first visit loads `require-gate` without
   running it. History lists the last
   20 actions of this session. Choosing one reopens its result, and
   "Restore inputs" puts its inputs back, asking first if you have
   unsaved edits.
3. **Editor.** A segmented control switches between Module, Case JSON,
   and Template. The editor has line numbers and syntax highlighting;
   Tab and Shift-Tab indent and outdent, and Enter keeps the
   indentation; press Escape, then Tab, to move focus out of the editor.
   About 700 ms after you stop typing in the module, the page posts it
   to `/api/check`: each diagnostic gets a wavy underline and a mark in
   the gutter, and its message appears under the line while the cursor
   or pointer is on it. Case JSON is checked as you type, with the line
   and column of the first error.
4. **Query, clocks, and actions.** The query field suggests the
   module's `query` names. `validAt` and `knownAt` must be RFC 3339.
   `Check`, `Run`, `Explore`, and `Render` post to the routes above.
   Ctrl or Cmd with Enter runs; adding Shift explores.
5. **Result.** Run and Explore results have three views: Opinion (the
   `opinion` sentences set as a printed page, with the execution mode,
   source trust, module, and `asOf`), Table (every field of the outcome
   and the report envelope), and JSON (the raw report, with Copy).
   Check shows `ok` or the diagnostics, each with a button that jumps to
   its line. Render shows the rendered text. Engine errors, invalid
   input, and an unreachable server are shown in place of a result.

Inputs, the chosen sample, and the chosen result view are kept in the
browser's local storage, so a reload keeps your work. `Explore` sends
the same body as `Run` and no separate `bounds` field; put finite
completions on the case JSON.

## See also

- [Getting started](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started.md)
- [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md)

### `POST /api/inputs`

Accepts `source` and `query` and returns `{ok: true, schema: ...}` with the input
schema derived from checked declarations, including evidence and effect request
metadata. Unsupported input representations return an explicit error. `/api/check`
diagnostic responses also include `locations` with source paths, byte spans and
UTF-16 editor ranges when available. These ranges identify the exact submitted
source; unavailable locations stay explicit.

========== https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md ==========

---
title: "Outcomes"
description: "Determinate, Suspended, Contingent, and the rest of the Fidryn outcome envelope."
url: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes"
markdown: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes.md"
author: "Bryan Gass"
---

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/outcomes
> This markdown mirror is for agents and plain-text readers.

# Outcomes

This guide explains the six honest results a Fidryn query can return.
Fidryn is a research interpreter. An outcome is not a court order, not
legal advice, and not a filing.

The six-kind result is a `fidryn.outcome/v0.1` object, defined by
[`schemas/outcome-v0.1.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/outcome-v0.1.json). Field names
are camelCase. Trust, coverage, execution mode, and assumptions that
cannot fit that schema live on the evaluation-report envelope
([`fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/schemas/evaluation-report-v0.2.json));
they are not extra keys on the outcome object (`additionalProperties`
is false).

See [CLI](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md), the [language grammar](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/grammar.ebnf), and
[Cases and time](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md).

## Envelope

CLI `run` / `explore` and mill `/api/run` / `/api/explore` emit
`fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2`. The six-kind legal result is nested as
`outcomeDocument`. That nested object is:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | `fidryn.outcome/v0.1`. |
| `module` | Compiled module identity, `Name@version`. |
| `sourceSnapshot` | Content identity of the compiled source snapshot, not the case's `module` string. |
| `query` | Query name you asked. |
| `asOf.validTime` | `--valid-at`. |
| `asOf.recordTime` | `--known-at`. |
| `modelBoundary.outsideScope` | Stable unique union of module `outside_scope` and case `outsideScope`. |
| `modelBoundary.admissibleCompletions` | The case's declared completion space when nonempty. |
| `outcome` | One of the six kinds below. |

`modelBoundary` is part of the answer. An omitted interpretation cannot
silently shrink the model after the fact: the envelope repeats the space
you declared. Read it before you treat a `determinate` value as "the"
result.

Unknown queries, exhausted fuel, and unsupported operations are engine
failures (exit 1). They are never rewritten as `inconsistent`.

## Evaluation report envelope

Qualifications that the outcome schema cannot carry live on
`fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2`. `fidryn_trace::render_checked_report`
requires an invocation-bound checked evaluation. The legacy `render_report`
API remains a v0.1 compatibility projection and does not supply a checked v0.2
invocation. `outcomeDocument` is the `fidryn.outcome/v0.1` projection
above; that schema is unchanged.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | `fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2`. |
| `executionMode` | `operative` or `scenario`. Operative `evaluate` does not apply `case.assumptions`. |
| `assumptions` | Overlay hypotheses copied onto a scenario report. Empty for operative runs. |
| `sourceTrust` | How the compiled source was authenticated. In-memory / mill pasted compile is `unauthenticated`. A path compile may be `fixture` or `byteVerified`. `fixture` is not byte-verified. |
| `verificationMethod` | `none` (no covering verification; a claims-digest binding is not covering), `structural` (shape only), or `finiteReplay` (each declared branch re-evaluated). Only `finiteReplay` is covering. |
| `coverage` | Optional `CoverageWitness`. Shape completeness is not covering meaning. |
| `outcomeDocument` | The `fidryn.outcome/v0.1` object from the previous section. |
| `invocation`, `invocationId` | Program/case identity, query arguments, clocks, execution mode, operation and actual operation budget. |
| `sourceBundle` | Identity of this compilation's immutable source observations. |
| `engineVersion`, `engineArtifact` | Engine semantics and, for CLI/mill reports, executable digest/size/platform/capture method. |
| `traceDocument` | Actual retained derivation nodes and parent links. |
| `searchEvidence` | Checked executed branches and exact coverage for exploration. |

Do not drop trust or coverage to keep an old outcome printer happy.
If a qualification cannot fit `fidryn.outcome/v0.1`, it belongs here.
A scenario report keeps `executionMode: scenario` and a nonempty
`assumptions` array on this envelope; it must not be reduced to an
outcome-only `fidryn.outcome/v0.1` export.

## Outcome kinds

`outcome` is tagged by `kind`. Every kind includes `trace`, a 32-character
hex `TraceId`. `fidryn explain TRACE_ID` loads `TRACE_ID.json` when that
file exists; otherwise it prints the hashed id. JSON traces always
include a `nodes` array. Saving the complete evaluation report preserves its
actual graph for a later `fidryn explain report.json`; a bare hash cannot
reconstruct discarded execution records.

Values inside an outcome are tagged runtime values
(`{"kind":"bool","data":true}`, `{"kind":"entity","data":"Bob"}`,
`{"kind":"unit"}`). They are not the looser case-JSON literals. A
proposition is `{"kind":"prop",...}`; it is not a boolean.

### Determinate

```json
{
  "kind": "determinate",
  "value": { "kind": "entity", "data": "Bob" },
  "trace": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "convergenceCertificate": null,
  "ignoredOpenIssues": []
}
```

**When.** The query has one answer that does not depend on any still-open
admissible completion, or a competent authority has already determined
the issue in this context. `Determinate` additionally requires a
**nonempty** exhaustive completion set. An empty declared domain is
`inconsistent` or `suspended`, never a vacuous `determinate`.

**Fields.**

- `value` (required). The answer. Compared with full value equality, not
  with display labels. `Bob` the entity is not `"Bob"` the string.
- `trace`. Provenance id for this evaluation.
- `convergenceCertificate`. Optional 32-hex completion-proof id. Present
  when a covering certificate was bound. A raw id cannot be deserialized
  back into a live certificate; the kernel has to verify it.
- `ignoredOpenIssues`. Open requests that were set aside. Nonempty only
  together with a **covering** certificate. A claims-digest binder is
  not enough; the constructor refuses `determinate` with ignored issues
  and a non-covering certificate.

> **What it is not.** Listing one alternative first is not determination.
> Hashing the open issues is not covering. Shape-complete `examined ==
> total` with empty or fabricated `branches` is not covering.

### Contingent

```json
{
  "kind": "contingent",
  "alternatives": {
    "i:SuccessorEligibility=I1": { "kind": "entity", "data": "Alice" },
    "i:SuccessorEligibility=I2": { "kind": "entity", "data": "Bob" }
  },
  "pivots": [],
  "trace": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

**When.** At least two still-admissible total answers disagree, or a
determinate branch is mixed with a nested contingent. Explore of the
trust fixture with two certificates and **no** recorded interpretation
is the usual example: I1 yields Alice, I2 yields Bob.

**Fields.**

- `alternatives` (required). Map from assignment identity (the full
  binding, not a list index) to the answer in that world.
- `pivots` (required). Open requests that split the worlds
  (`needInterpretation`, `needChoice`, `needEvidence`, and so on).
- `trace`.

Aggregation compares full `Value`s. Two worlds that print the same label
but differ in kind stay contingent. A determinate world plus a
contingent world is contingent, not determinate.

### Suspended

```json
{
  "kind": "suspended",
  "requests": [
    {
      "kind": "needInterpretation",
      "source": "Instrument.clause(\"4.4\")",
      "family": "SuccessorEligibility"
    }
  ],
  "trace": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

**When.** The evaluator needs a legal operation that the case does not
discharge, and there is no covering certificate that would let those
open branches be ignored. `run` never invents the missing completion.
Open branches without a covering certificate stay `suspended`.

Typical causes: missing evidence whose `observedAt` is at or before
known-at; a judgment with no matching determination; a choice with no
recorded decision; an interpretation family with no recorded
alternative; a unique-occupant query with no occupancy; a closed-world
status asked without a closure record; an incomplete explore that ran
out of budget.

**Fields.**

- `requests` (required). The outstanding `OpenRequest` set.
- `trace`.

Request kinds you will see:

| `kind` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `needEvidence` | `issue` plus `schema`. Observe matches that schema and known-at. |
| `needJudgment` | `issue` (a proposition term) plus `protocol`. Determine matches protocol and issue. |
| `needChoice` | `protocol` plus `options`. |
| `needInterpretation` | `source` plus `family`. |
| `needApplicableLaw` | `issue` plus `candidates`. A unique candidate may resume; a tie suspends. |
| `needConflict` | `graph` plus `doctrines`. A unique applicable doctrine may resume; list order is never a tie-break. |
| `needCustom` | `effect` plus `payload` (for example an incomplete explore). |

### NormConflict

```json
{
  "kind": "normConflict",
  "doctrines": [ { "name": "LaterInTime" } ],
  "trace": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

**When.** Staged effects disagree and the conflict oracle cannot pick
exactly one applicable doctrine. Zero applicable doctrines, or two or
more incompatible ones, stay unresolved. Silent preference for the
first name in a list is forbidden.

**Fields.**

- `doctrines` (required). The conflict doctrines involved (`name`,
  `guard`, `defeats`, `as_to`, `reason`, and identity metadata).
- `trace`.

If a unique doctrine applies, evaluation resumes instead of returning
this kind. Recorded resolutions on the case, when present, also resume.

### OutsideCompetence

```json
{
  "kind": "outsideCompetence",
  "request": {
    "kind": "needInterpretation",
    "source": "Instrument.clause(\"4.4\")",
    "family": "SuccessorEligibility"
  },
  "reason": "recorded interpretation is not in the admissible set",
  "trace": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

**When.** The case asks the interpreter to do something outside the
declared model or the module's competence. A recorded interpretation or
choice that is not in `admissibleCompletions` is the usual case. An
explored doctrine or source outside the candidate set is another.

**Fields.**

- `request` (required). The operation that could not be discharged.
- `reason` (required). Why it is outside competence, not merely open.
- `trace`.

`established: false` from a competent protocol is a negative
determination, not this kind.

### Inconsistent

```json
{
  "kind": "inconsistent",
  "core": ["empty completion set"],
  "trace": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

**When.** The admitted model cannot be satisfied. Examples: a named
interpretation family whose declared list is empty; every explored
branch unsatisfiable; two established occupants of an office that must
be unique.

**Fields.**

- `core` (required). Human-readable inconsistency lines. Explore of an
  empty declared domain uses `empty completion set`.
- `trace`.

Engine errors are not this kind. `unknown query q` exits without an
outcome document.

## Rules to internalize

### Determinate needs nonempty exhaustive agreement or a competent determination

A legal computation may return one determinate result only when that
result is invariant across every still-admissible resolution, or when a
competent authority has already made a determination that is operative
in the relevant context. The completion set those worlds are drawn from
must be nonempty and exhaustive. Vacuity (`Family: []`) is not
agreement. `run` does not choose a completion to manufacture agreement.

### Open branches without a covering certificate stay Suspended

An open `needInterpretation`, `needEvidence`, or similar request is not
dropped because the rest of the query looks settled. Ignoring open
issues on a `determinate` result requires `ignoredOpenIssues` **and** a
covering `convergenceCertificate`. Without that pair, the outcome is
`suspended`.

### A claims digest is not covering proof

`CheckedCertificate::verified` binds a proof id to a hash of program,
snapshot, case, query, clocks, constraints, and answer. Matching that
digest does not discharge open constraints and does not set
`covering: true`.

Covering requires `verified_covering` plus a complete
`CoverageWitness`: `incomplete == false`, `examined == total`,
`examined > 0`, matching answer, and a `branches` list whose meaning
checks. Shape completeness is not enough.
`fidryn-kernel::accept_covering_eval` re-evaluates each
`CoverageWitness.branches` entry (`BranchClaim { bindings, answer }`)
against the claimed program and query. It rejects fabricated
evaluations, duplicate worlds, incomplete or mismatched counts, and
digest-only certificates. The kernel does not search and does not
invent worlds. `accept_covering` (shape only) is not that check.

### explore versus run

`run` evaluates the given case with a `CaseFile` handler. Missing
completions suspend. It never fills I1 or I2 for you.

`explore` searches the declared `admissibleCompletions` (and any
`--bounds` merge). Recorded interpretations and decisions constrain the
search; they are not overwritten. Divergent total answers become
`contingent`. Convergent nonempty answers can become `determinate`. An
empty named domain becomes `inconsistent`.

The two commands need not return the same category. With two
certificates and an open `SuccessorEligibility` domain,
`run ... --query acting_trustee` suspends (`needInterpretation`) while
`explore` is `contingent` between Alice and Bob. With
[`court-selects-i2.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/examples/trust/cases/court-selects-i2.json),
both answer Bob, because I2 is already on the case and inside the
declared domain. Treat agreement as a fact about that record, not as a
reason to skip reading `kind`.

### modelBoundary is on the envelope

Do not read `outcome.value` and ignore `modelBoundary`.
`outsideScope` is the union of module and case exclusions; a case that
lists only `tax` does not erase the module's `creditor_priority`.
`admissibleCompletions` on the envelope is the space the result is
relative to. If you omitted a family, the result is silent about that
family; it is not a proof that the family does not matter.

### Prop is not Bool

`Prop` is a first-class sort. There is no conversion from a proposition
term to `bool`. `Incapacitated(Bryan, Administer(BRT))` is not `true`.
Guards use `operative`, `assumed`, `determined`, or `necessarily`. A
tagged `{ "kind": "bool", "data": false }` is boolean; a tagged
`{ "kind": "prop", "data": { "predicate": "Incapacitated", "arguments": [] } }`
is not. Case JSON that needs both field names `kind` and `data` for a
user record must use `{ "kind": "record", "data": { ... } }`; see
[Cases and time](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cases-and-time.md).

## Reading a result

1. Confirm the CLI/mill report `schema` is
   `fidryn.evaluation-report/v0.2`, then open nested `outcomeDocument`
   (`schema` `fidryn.outcome/v0.1`). Read `executionMode`,
   `sourceTrust`, and `assumptions` on the report before treating the
   answer as operative.
2. Read `modelBoundary` and `asOf` before `outcome.kind`.
3. Branch on `kind`. Only `determinate` has `value` as *the* answer.
4. If `kind` is `determinate` and `ignoredOpenIssues` is nonempty, demand
   a covering certificate, not a hex string you minted yourself.
5. If `kind` is `suspended` or `contingent`, the work is in `requests` /
   `pivots` and `alternatives`, not in guessing a default.
6. Do not promote a `run` suspension into the `explore` contingent
   answer, or the reverse, without a new evaluation.

The modules under `examples/` and the records under `tests/` are
fixtures for this interpreter. They are not legal advice.

========== https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/examples.md ==========

---
title: "Examples"
description: "Trust, tax, federal slices, and the fifty-state corpus map for Fidryn."

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/examples
> This markdown mirror is for agents and plain-text readers.

# Example corpus

This catalog is a map of the Fidryn example tree. The modules under
`examples/` and the independent programs under `tests/programs/` are
research fixtures. They are not legal advice, not operative instruments,
and not a complete statement of any jurisdiction's law.

Build the toolchain as in [getting-started](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/getting-started.md). Source
syntax is in [language](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/language.md). Subcommands, timestamps, and
outcome envelopes are in [cli](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md). Commands below assume the
repository root as the working directory. The binary name is `fidryn`.
From a checkout that has not installed the binary, prefix the same
subcommands with `cargo run -p fidryn-cli --`.

## How to use an example

Every module is a `.fr` file. Start by checking it. `check` authenticates
the declared source manifest (when the module has one), elaborates, and
type-checks. A clean module prints `ok`.

<!-- examples-status:begin -->
`fidryn check` passes for 54 of the 114 `.fr` modules under `examples/`, `packages/`, `prelude/` and `tests/programs/` with this version. The [per-file list](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/examples/STATUS.md) is generated by `cargo xtask examples --update`. A file marked (draft) does not pass and cannot be run; [implementation status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md) lists what the language cannot yet express.
<!-- examples-status:end -->

```sh
fidryn check examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr
```

If the directory contains a `cases/` folder, those files are
`fidryn.case-record/v0.1` JSON records. `run` evaluates one named query
against one record at a pair of ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamps. `run`
never chooses a completion. A `Suspended` outcome is an honest result,
not a failed command.

```sh
fidryn run examples/us-federal/flsa/flsa.fr \
  --query overtime_hours \
  --case examples/us-federal/flsa/cases/forty-one-hours.json \
  --valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00 \
  --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00
```

`--valid-at` is the legal valid time. `--known-at` is the record time.
Evidence whose `observedAt` is after `--known-at` does not discharge a
query. `--arg KEY=VALUE` writes `case.facts["KEY"]` on top of the JSON
(for example `--arg provision=ChildSupportWaiver`).

State modules under `examples/states/` do not ship a companion JSON case
record or a JSON source manifest. Their `scenario` blocks write down
example facts, but the interpreter does not read them: a run takes its
facts from a case record. The `source { ... }` block carries the
citation, artifact, and `digest fixture`, and no file is read from it
(see [implementation status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md)). Check the
module:

```sh
fidryn check examples/states/florida/homestead.fr
```

`verify` cannot yet discharge the honesty assertions in these modules. It
reports the property `unknown` and exits with status 1:

```sh exit=1
fidryn verify examples/states/florida/homestead.fr --property HomesteadHonesty
```

A query that looks mechanical (deadlines, dollar caps, day counts,
acreage) is `automatic` or `Evaluate` with an empty effect row. A query
that needs a tribunal, agency, or open-textured standard uses `Determine`
or `Observe` and must be allowed to `Suspend`. The fixtures do not hide
judgment in a Boolean.

## Start here

These eleven modules cover an instrument, a closed-form tax slice, an
agency procedure, a formation filing, a family agreement, a civil-procedure
spine, a consumer clock, a state constitutional cap, a federal wage rule,
and two interpreter programs. The rows not marked (draft) check clean.

| Path | Purpose | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr` | Successor trustee occupancy under the Bryan revocable-trust fixture. | `fidryn check examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr` |
| `examples/tax/federal-tax.fr` | Closed-form ordinary-income tax and FinCEN BOI after the domestic-company exemption. | `fidryn check examples/tax/federal-tax.fr` |
| `examples/foia/foia-request.fr` | FOIA request processing; a proposed Exemption 5 withholding still needs harm and segregability. | `fidryn check examples/foia/foia-request.fr` |
| `examples/massachusetts-llc/harbor-robotics.fr` | Massachusetts LLC formation; a transport receipt is not an official filing record. | `fidryn check examples/massachusetts-llc/harbor-robotics.fr` |
| `examples/prenup/ava-noah.fr` | California UPAA provision enforcement for the Ava–Noah agreement. | `fidryn check examples/prenup/ava-noah.fr` |
| `examples/procedure/civil-complaint.fr` | FRCP 3/4/12/58 complaint-to-judgment spine. | `fidryn check examples/procedure/civil-complaint.fr` |
| `examples/california/security-deposit/security-deposit.fr` (draft) | California 21-day security-deposit return clock versus bad-faith doubling. | not runnable |
| `examples/states/florida/homestead.fr` | Florida homestead acreage caps and forced-sale character. Its `scenario` blocks are not read by the interpreter. | `fidryn check examples/states/florida/homestead.fr` |
| `examples/us-federal/flsa/flsa.fr` | FLSA 40-hour overtime versus the white-collar exemption. | `fidryn check examples/us-federal/flsa/flsa.fr` |
| `tests/programs/require-gate.fr` | `require true` returns 7; `require false` does not run the return. | `fidryn check tests/programs/require-gate.fr` |
| `tests/programs/late-payment.fr` | Invoice duty, timely-payment decision, and a strict-versus-extended deadline family. | `fidryn check tests/programs/late-payment.fr` |

Run the clean modules that ship JSON case records. Each command's
timestamps are the latest `observedAt` among the record's evidence, or
the module's `recorded_at` when the record has no evidence.

```sh
fidryn run examples/trust/bryan-revocable-trust.fr \
  --query acting_trustee \
  --case examples/trust/cases/one-certificate.json \
  --valid-at 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z \
  --known-at 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z
```

Other trust records in the same folder are
`bob-plus-open-alice.json`, `two-certificates-open-eligibility.json`, and
`court-selects-i2.json`. One physician certificate without a checked
completion is expected to suspend.

```sh
fidryn run examples/tax/federal-tax.fr \
  --query tax_on \
  --case examples/tax/cases/ordinary-income.json \
  --valid-at 2026-08-14T00:00:00-04:00 \
  --known-at 2026-08-14T00:00:00-04:00
```

```sh
fidryn run examples/tax/federal-tax.fr \
  --query boi_required \
  --case examples/tax/cases/domestic-company-after-exemption.json \
  --valid-at 2026-09-01T00:00:00-04:00 \
  --known-at 2026-09-01T00:00:00-04:00
```

Under its consequence, the exemption rule of `federal-tax.fr` writes
`valid_time [2026-08-14, +inf)` and a `record_time` line. Fidryn 0.3 reads
such lines and does not apply them (see
`the_valid_time_and_record_time_lines_of_a_rule_are_not_applied` under
[Known limits pinned by tests](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md#known-limits-pinned-by-tests)).
So the answer, `false`, is the same for
`--valid-at 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z`, long before the interval begins.

```sh
fidryn run examples/foia/foia-request.fr \
  --query disposition \
  --case examples/foia/cases/proposed-exemption-5-withholding.json \
  --valid-at 2026-08-23T12:00:00-04:00 \
  --known-at 2026-08-23T12:00:00-04:00
```

```sh
fidryn run examples/massachusetts-llc/harbor-robotics.fr \
  --query entity_status \
  --case examples/massachusetts-llc/cases/official-filing-record.json \
  --valid-at 2026-08-28T14:12:00-04:00 \
  --known-at 2026-08-28T14:12:00-04:00
```

`examples/massachusetts-llc/cases/transmitted-without-official-record.json`
is the contrast case: transmission without an `OfficialFilingRecord`
suspends.

Under its consequence, the formation rule of `harbor-robotics.fr` writes
`valid_time [effective_at, +inf)` and a `record_time` line, and they are
not applied either. The answer, `FormedLLC`, is the same for
`--valid-at 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z`, long before the filing. It does depend
on `--known-at`, through the filing record of the case: with a
`--known-at` before 14:12 that day the record is not yet known, and the
answer is `NotFormedLLC`.

```sh
fidryn run examples/prenup/ava-noah.fr \
  --query provision_result \
  --case examples/prenup/cases/divorce-record.json \
  --valid-at 2026-08-23T12:00:00-07:00 \
  --known-at 2026-08-23T12:00:00-07:00
```

`divorce-record-without-enforceability-order.json` suspends on
`PrenupEnforceability`. `--arg provision=ChildSupportWaiver` overwrites
`case.facts["provision"]` when you want a different clause without
editing the JSON.

```sh
fidryn run examples/procedure/civil-complaint.fr \
  --query judgment \
  --case examples/procedure/cases/judgment-entered.json \
  --valid-at 2026-10-01T16:00:00-04:00 \
  --known-at 2026-10-01T16:00:00-04:00
```

`complaint-answered-without-judgment.json` suspends because there is no
judgment entry.

```sh
fidryn run examples/us-federal/flsa/flsa.fr \
  --query overtime_hours \
  --case examples/us-federal/flsa/cases/forty-one-hours.json \
  --valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00 \
  --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00
```

Florida homestead has no JSON case file, and the interpreter does not read
its `scenario` blocks (`InsideCityHalfAcre`, `RuralHundredSixty`,
`TaxCreditor`), so this guide never passes it to `fidryn run`.
`require-gate.fr` and `late-payment.fr` have no case records of their
own; they run with the empty case record that `tests/programs/` ships.
See [Independent programs](#independent-programs).

## Federal slices

Bounded United States Code and CFR slices live under
`examples/us-federal/`. Fidryn does not contain the United States Code.
The catalog module at `examples/us-federal/catalog/usc-titles.fr` records
that fact. Each slice names the dated source it encodes and lists what it
leaves `outside_scope`.

Unless a row says otherwise, these modules use the 2026-09-17 snapshot
and this timestamp pair:

```
--valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00 --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00
```

Check, then run:

```text
fidryn check PATH
fidryn run PATH --query QUERY --case CASE \
  --valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00 \
  --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00
```

The original FOIA spine is `examples/foia/foia-request.fr`, not under
`us-federal/`. It is in [Start here](#start-here).

### Litigators, every week

| Path | Purpose | Query | Case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `examples/us-federal/diversity/diversity.fr` | 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a). The $75,000 amount-in-controversy floor is mechanical; complete diversity is not. | `amount_in_controversy_met` | `examples/us-federal/diversity/cases/amount-met-diversity-open.json` |
| `examples/us-federal/removal/removal.fr` (draft) | 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b). Thirty-day removal clock versus later-served-defendant doctrine. | `thirty_day_window` | `examples/us-federal/removal/cases/inside-thirty-days.json` |
| `examples/us-federal/hearsay/hearsay.fr` | Fed. R. Evid. 801–804. Out-of-court use versus the 803(6) business-records exception. | `out_of_court` | `examples/us-federal/hearsay/cases/out-of-court-statement.json` |
| `examples/us-federal/speedy-trial/speedy-trial.fr` (draft) | 18 U.S.C. § 3161. Seventy-day clock versus ends-of-justice continuance. | `seventy_day_window` | `examples/us-federal/speedy-trial/cases/inside-seventy-days.json` |

### Catalog

`examples/us-federal/catalog/usc-titles.fr` (`US.Federal.Code.Catalog`)
does not encode titles. It records that the United States Code, the CFR,
uncodified statutes, case law, and internal guidance remain outside this
corpus except for the slices listed above.

```sh
fidryn check examples/us-federal/catalog/usc-titles.fr
fidryn run examples/us-federal/catalog/usc-titles.fr --query complete_code_is_outside_scope --case examples/us-federal/catalog/cases/catalog-query.json --valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00 --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00-04:00
```

## Fifty-state corpus

`examples/states/` has one module per U.S. state. Each encodes part of
the state law named in its principal citation in the table below, on
topics such as homestead, final pay, security deposits, paid leave,
no-fault insurance and community property. These are research fixtures,
not legal advice, and not a complete statement of any state's code.

There is no companion JSON case file and no JSON source manifest. The
`scenario` blocks in each `.fr` file write down example facts, but the
interpreter does not read them; a run takes its facts from a case
record. `source_manifest` is omitted, so the compiler uses an empty
manifest. The `source { ... }` block, which carries the citation,
artifact, and `digest fixture`, does not take the manifest's place: no
file is read from it.

The quality bar for writing a state module is
`examples/states/florida/homestead.fr` (`Florida.Property.Homestead`,
Fla. Const. art. X, § 4). It passes the checker. Urban acreage 0.5, rural
acreage 160, and the $1,000 personal-property cap are `automatic`.
Homestead character and excepted-creditor status stay in `Determine` /
`Observe`. Scenarios `InsideCityHalfAcre`, `RuralHundredSixty`, and
`TaxCreditor` sit in the same file. Fixture excerpts live next to each
module under `sources/` and are not official editions.

```sh
fidryn check examples/states/florida/homestead.fr
```

District of Columbia and the territories are outside this corpus.

## Independent programs

`tests/programs/` holds small modules that exercise the interpreter.
They are not jurisdiction slices. They declare `outside_scope`. The
directory ships an empty case record, `tests/programs/cases/empty.json`,
with no facts, evidence or completions. Every query in these programs
runs against it and exits 0; a query that needs something the record
does not hold is suspended. Check them:

```sh
fidryn check tests/programs/eligibility-succession.fr
fidryn check tests/programs/named-decision.fr
fidryn check tests/programs/two-offices.fr
fidryn check tests/programs/require-gate.fr
fidryn check tests/programs/late-payment.fr
fidryn check tests/programs/late-payment-extended.fr
fidryn check tests/programs/transaction-atomic.fr
```

Run one against the empty case record:

```sh
fidryn run tests/programs/late-payment.fr \
  --query obligation_status \
  --case tests/programs/cases/empty.json \
  --valid-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z \
  --known-at 2026-09-17T12:00:00Z
```

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/programs/eligibility-succession.fr` | `UniqueOccupant` for `TrusteeOf(BRT)` under competing `SuccessorEligibility` interpretations. Query `acting_trustee`. |
| `tests/programs/named-decision.fr` | `RunDecision` on `ProcessResponsiveRecord`; the observation is required. Query `q`. |
| `tests/programs/two-offices.fr` | Two independent offices, trustee and executor, each with its own eligibility family. Queries `acting_trustee` and `acting_executor`. |
| `tests/programs/require-gate.fr` | Query `q` is `require true; return 7`. Query `r` is `require false; return 7`. False require does not run the return. |
| `tests/programs/late-payment.fr` | `PayInvoice` duty, `TimelyPayment` decision, and `DeadlineMeaning` (strict versus 15 counted days). Queries `due`, `paid_on_time`, `obligation_status`. |
| `tests/programs/late-payment-extended.fr` | Same duty shape with `due 15 counted_days after invoice_date` and no competing deadline family. |
| `tests/programs/transaction-atomic.fr` | `transaction` block that attaches then discharges a `pay` duty; query `q` is declared `-> DutyStatus`. Partial surface — not a general transaction engine. |

## Honesty

These fixtures are not legal advice and not a complete code. Read each
module's `outside_scope` before treating an answer as even a research
result.

**`outside_scope`.** Every module names the topics, titles, doctrines,
and procedures it does not encode. Outcomes carry that boundary. An
omitted interpretation cannot silently shrink the model.

**`digest fixture`.** Source blocks on the 2026-09-17 slices use
`digest fixture`. That is a fixture trust profile, not byte-verified
authentication of the artifact, and not an official edition. Excerpts
under each module's `sources/` directory end by saying they are not
official editions.

**Not the United States Code.** The United States Code is a codification
of statutes, not the whole of federal law. Regulations, case law,
internal guidance, and uncodified provisions sit elsewhere. This corpus
encodes bounded slices of the law. `US.Federal.Code.Catalog` exists so
the interpreter cannot honestly claim completeness.

`run` never chooses a completion. Open-textured queries must be allowed
to `Suspend`. The kernel does not search.
