---
title: "Coverage"
description: "The coverage ledger of the sample of the United States Code in the Fidryn repository: what was imported, addressed and extracted."
url: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/coverage"
markdown: "https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/coverage.md"
author: "Bryan Gass"
---

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/coverage
> This markdown mirror is for agents and plain-text readers.

# Coverage

The figures on this page are those of the sample of the United States Code
committed in this repository, under `samples/uscode/`, and of nothing else.
The sample holds three whole titles of the release `119-142` of the
official XML release point published by the Office of the Law Revision
Counsel: Title 1, Title 11 Appendix and Title 45. The table below is
generated from the coverage ledger of the sample's workspace,
[`samples/uscode/workspace/coverage.json`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/samples/uscode/workspace/coverage.json),
which [`fidryn coverage`](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/cli.md#coverage) prints and
[The coverage ledger](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#the-coverage-ledger) describes key by
key.

## What the words mean

The ledger says how far the provisions of the sample are taken in three
words, and in no others.

- **Imported.** The official text of the provision is in a module, read
  from a pinned file, the publisher's archive, whose size and digests the
  importer verifies against the retrieval record that says where and when
  it was fetched. The lock of the workspace records the digests of each
  archive and of each module file, and the check of the workspace verifies
  every module file against them.
- **Addressed.** The provision has a typed address, and its place in the
  hierarchy, its status and the references in its text are resolved and
  checked. Every provision imported is addressed. Each reference has an
  outcome, and the table gives the references of each layer by outcome, so
  that a reader sees how many of them reach their target.
- **Classified.** What kind of provision it is, is recorded. At this version
  the one kind that is recorded is a definition, and the ledger gives the
  number of definitions extracted, by basis and by kind. It gives no count
  of classified provisions, since one provision can hold more than one
  definition.

## The basis of a definition

Each definition extracted has one of three bases:

- `enacted`: its reach names a region of the Code, and the file of its unit
  declares its title positive law, so the words that state the reach are
  those the law enacted.
- `restated`: its reach names a region of the Code, and the file of its
  unit does not declare its title positive law, so the words are those of
  the editors of the Code, and the reach the law enacted may differ from the
  one they state.
- `unresolved`: the rules found no region of the Code for it, for one of
  four causes: it states no reach that they read; its reach is a link to a
  law outside the Code, such as a public law; its reach words are in a form
  the rules do not resolve, whatever they name: a part of the Code, as "this
  chapter and chapter 5" and, of a court rule, "this Rule 3021" do, or a law
  outside it, as "this Act" does; or
  its reach is in a form they resolve, "this" and the name of a kind of
  provision or container, but neither the provision that states the reach
  nor any provision or container above it is of that kind, as with "As
  used in this subtitle" in a section that stands in no subtitle.

The rules read definitions written in a closed list of forms
([Definitions](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#definitions)), and they do not find every
definition that the text holds. The share of the definitions they miss has
not been measured for the sample.

## Counted and not imported

Some of what the publisher's files hold is by rule not imported. The
importer counts it in the lock of the workspace under these six names, and
the ledger copies the counts:

- `tables_of_contents`: the tables of contents, whose entries repeat the
  headings of the units they list;
- `footnotes_in_tables_of_contents`: the footnotes inside them;
- `links_in_tables_of_contents`: the links inside them;
- `release_notes`: the notes that say which release a file is current
  through;
- `links_without_words`: the links that have no words, or white space
  alone;
- `note_group_headings`: the cross headings that open the groups of notes,
  whose labels are not imported; what a cross heading holds after its label
  is imported, as a note of its group.

## The figures

<!-- coverage-table:begin -->

| Counted | Key | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Units, by kind | `totals.units_by_kind` | 229 `courtRule`, 1 `level`, 333 `section` |
| Units, by status (`in-force` for a unit with none) | `totals.units_by_status` | 482 `in-force`, 9 `omitted`, 68 `repealed`, 4 `transferred` |
| Containers imported | `totals.containers` | 72 |

| Definitions extracted, by kind | `totals.definitions_by_kind` | 7 `borrowed`, 1 `does_not_include`, 15 `includes`, 121 `means` |
| Counted and not imported | `totals.not_imported` | 19 `tables_of_contents`, 4 `footnotes_in_tables_of_contents`, 341 `links_in_tables_of_contents`, 3 `release_notes`, 0 `links_without_words`, 358 `note_group_headings` |
| The file `usc01.xml` (positive law) | `by_source.0` | 39 units, 129 provisions, 10 definitions |
| The file `usc11a.xml` (not positive law) | `by_source.1` | 230 units, 2,362 provisions, 4 definitions |
| The file `usc45.xml` (not positive law) | `by_source.2` | 294 units, 2,366 provisions, 130 definitions |

<!-- coverage-table:end -->

`cargo xtask uscode-sample --update` writes this table from the ledger, and
`cargo xtask uscode-sample`, which `cargo xtask ci` runs, fails when the
table is not what the ledger gives.

---
title: "Contributing"

> Canonical HTML: https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/contributing

# Contributing to Fidryn

This file is for people building the 0.3 reference interpreter. It is
not a language tutorial and not legal advice. Product usage lives in
the [README](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/README.md) and the [documentation hub](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/index.md).

Fidryn (FID-rin) is a research fixture. Modules under `examples/` and
records under `tests/` exercise the interpreter. They are not operative
instruments and not a complete statement of any jurisdiction's law.

Fidryn is released under the MIT License. Licensing and contribution
rights are described in [Licensing](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/LICENSING.md). Contributions are
accepted under the same license; no separate agreement is required.

## Toolchain

Rust 1.98, edition 2024. Workspace `package.rust-version` is 1.98.
[`rust-toolchain.toml`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/rust-toolchain.toml) pins the 1.98.1
channel and the `rustfmt` and `clippy` components.

If `cargo` or `git` pick the wrong tools on this Mac, a working PATH is
`/opt/homebrew/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`, with
`DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`.
[`.cargo/config.toml`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/.cargo/config.toml) already points the linker
at Command Line Tools clang because the Xcode license is unsigned.

## Checks

From the repository root:

```
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked --offline -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked --offline
```

`cargo xtask ci --fmt` runs, in this order, formatting, the complete Rust
tests and Clippy, Rustdoc with warnings denied, executable schema probes,
Python lint/format/types, the conformance tests of `conformance/` (given the
built binary in `FIDRYN_BINARY`, since the comparison of two releases and the
check of a law repository there run it), the sample check
(`cargo xtask uscode-sample`: the committed archives of the Code against
their retrieval record, the committed workspace against what the importer
writes from them on one worker and on eight, its check and its coverage
ledger, the committed profile and its counts against the script that counts
the archives, the check and the ledger, the text of every provision and note
against what an independent script reads from the publisher's XML, the
definitions of the workspace against what a second implementation of the
definition rules finds in the archives, the
curated sample, checked with the generated one as its dependency, every
citation of it `exact` and its binding not stale, and the table of the
coverage page against the ledger), generated-site consistency, the example
status and documentation checks described below, required JavaScript tests,
and benchmark compilation. Node, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and the
commands `git`, `bash`, `jq`, `sha256sum` and `tar`, which the tests run, are
required for qualification.
`uv run --locked` uses `.python-version` and `uv.lock`.

GitHub runs this gate for pushes and PRs to `dev` and `main`, plus separate
Linux/macOS/Windows tests, dependency auditing, secret scanning, workflow linting
and CodeQL. The workflow `Law integration`, which checks a law repository
with the toolchain of a commit, runs only when it is started by hand
([Checking a law repository](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/development.md#checking-a-law-repository)).
Development and native branch protections are described in
[Development and promotion](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/development.md). Generated environments and build
outputs are not committed.

Do not weaken no-false-determinacy to make a test pass.

## Website

The public site in [`site/`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/tree/main/site/) is generated from these guides
by the workspace task runner. After editing a guide in `docs/`, run:

```
cargo xtask site
```

and commit the markdown together with the regenerated files under
`site/`. `cargo xtask site --check` fails when the committed site is
stale, and `cargo xtask ci` runs that check. The landing page's
specimen is evaluated by the real interpreter at build time, so a
change in semantics also makes the site stale.

The stylesheet and script in `site/assets/` are written by hand. The
mill, whose page lives in [`web/`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/tree/main/web/), embeds the stylesheet
`fidryn.css` and has its own script, `web/mill.js`. `cargo xtask ci` requires Node to run the JavaScript unit tests in
`web/tests/`; Node is not needed to build or serve the interpreter.

## Example status and documentation checks

`cargo xtask examples` runs `fidryn check` on every `.fr` file under
`examples/`, `packages/`, `prelude/` and `tests/programs/`, and fails when
the recorded result is out of date. The record is `examples/status.json`
and `examples/STATUS.md`; the status sentence between the
`examples-status` markers in `README.md`, `examples/README.md`,
`examples/states/README.md` and `docs/examples.md`; and the ` (draft)`
mark after each path of a failing file that `README.md`,
`examples/README.md`, `examples/states/README.md` or a Markdown file
directly under `docs/` mentions outside a code block. Do not edit any of these by
hand. `cargo xtask examples --update` rewrites the status files, the
status sentences and the draft marks. Run `cargo xtask site` after it,
because the site is generated from the guides it rewrites.

`cargo xtask docs` reads the Markdown in `README.md`, `LICENSING.md`,
`CHANGELOG.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `docs/`, `examples/`, `packages/`,
`conformance/`, `samples/` and `site/README.md`. It checks that every
relative link resolves, that every untagged or `fidryn`-tagged code block
that starts with `module` passes the checker, that every such block whose
first line that is not blank is `edition 2` passes the checks of one law
module ([Law modules](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/law-modules.md#editions)), and that the `fidryn`
commands in blocks tagged `sh` behave as the tag says. `--skip-commands`
leaves out the commands.

A code block that shows a `fidryn` command takes one of these tags:

- `sh`: the check runs each `fidryn` command in the block from the
  repository root and expects exit status 0. A command is a line, with
  lines ending in `\` joined, that starts with `fidryn` or with
  `cargo run -p fidryn-cli --`; the check runs the built `fidryn` binary
  with the words after that prefix. A line in an `sh` block that is not a
  `fidryn` command, such as `cargo test --workspace --locked`, is not run.
  A command with `ui` as one of its words is taken to start the mill, so
  it is not run either. The check does not use a shell, so a command
  must not use `>`, `>>`, `<`, `|`, `&&`, `||` or `;`. A command that has
  not exited after 60 seconds is stopped and reported.
- `sh exit=N`: the same, but each command must exit with status `N`. A
  tag whose first word is `sh` and which is neither `sh` nor `sh exit=N`
  with `N` an integer, such as `sh exit 1`, is reported.
- `text`: the block is shown and not run. Use it for placeholders such as
  `PATH`, for output redirection, and for commands that cannot run
  unattended.

A block with any other tag, such as `shell`, or with none, must not show
a `fidryn` command. Such a tag is not itself reported, but a block under
it that shows a `fidryn` command is reported as an untagged block would
be.

## Pipeline

Land a change in the crate that owns that stage:

```
syntax → hir → check → core → eval → handlers → verify → driver → cli
```

`fidryn-kernel` sits beside verify: it accepts or rejects covering
claims and does not search. `fidryn-trace`, `fidryn-solve`,
`fidryn-adapt`, and `fidryn-render` support the pipeline; they are not
extra stages.

Do not add reverse dependencies. Do not put evaluator logic in
`syntax`. Do not put parser logic in `core`. `fidryn-driver` must not
depend on `fidryn-cli`.

## Crates

Workspace members are listed in [`Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/Cargo.toml).

```
fidryn-syntax          lossless CST, parser, formatter
fidryn-core            IR, types, Outcome, LegalState, diagnostics
fidryn-hir             names, imports, elaboration  (syntax + core)
fidryn-check           types, effects, authority, time, strata (hir + core); edition 2 lowering and one-module check (syntax + provision)
fidryn-eval            worklist evaluator (core)
fidryn-handlers        CaseFile, Scenario, Explore, Skeptical (core + eval)
fidryn-verify          bounded explorer and invariants (eval + handlers)
fidryn-kernel          covering-check boundary (accept/reject; no proof gen)
fidryn-driver          incremental check/run memo; workspace check, writer and change sets (provision)
fidryn-trace           DAG, canonical JSON, source maps (core)
fidryn-render          constrained templates (missing keys fail closed)
fidryn-adapt           capability-gated filing adapters
fidryn-solve           bounded DPLL over declared finite domains
fidryn-provision       law-module model and the rules over it (no workspace crate)
fidryn-ingest-uscode   official XML release point into law modules (provision)
fidryn-cli             fidryn binary and localhost mill; ingest, text, coverage and changes commands (driver + provision + ingest-uscode)
```

## Tests

Tests live next to the crates they exercise (`#[cfg(test)]` in `src`,
and `crates/<name>/tests/` when a crate has an integration kit).

The adversarial review kit is
[`tests/integration/adversarial_regressions.rs`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/tests/integration/adversarial_regressions.rs).
Those tests are regressions, not closure of the language.

Independent programs live under [`tests/programs/`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/tree/main/tests/programs/).
[`crates/fidryn-verify/tests/domains.rs`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/crates/fidryn-verify/tests/domains.rs)
runs them as independently named modules. Do not rewrite compiled Core
to green fingerprint tests. Patching a `CoreModule` so a digest, plan,
or outcome matches is not a passing test.

## Commits

Write each commit subject as an imperative sentence with no type prefix,
for example `Require code-scanning findings to pass before promotion`.
Recent history follows this; older commits used Conventional Commits
prefixes such as `feat(syntax):`, which are no longer used. Prefer atomic
commits in pipeline order, then tests and docs. Do not dump unrelated
crates into one commit.

## Grammar

The grammar is [`grammar.ebnf`](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/grammar.ebnf) at the repository root.
It is closed, but the 0.3 parser enforces closed field sets only in
`source` blocks, rule bodies and judgment request blocks. In most other
declarations an unknown field is skipped without a diagnostic; see
[implementation status](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md).

## Implementer documents

These files are crate contracts and evidence. They are not user
tutorials.

- [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — Frozen crate graph, public APIs, and the pipeline of total functions over trees.
- [implementation-status.md](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/implementation-status.md) — What the 0.3 interpreter does and does not do, each statement backed by a test or a code location. A `.fr` file is not an executable specification.

The internal working ledgers are indexed in
[internal/README.md](https://github.com/BeeGass/fidryn/blob/main/docs/internal/README.md). They are not reader
documentation, and parts of them describe earlier states of the code.

Mill HTTP routes are documented in [mill.md](https://fidryn.onlygass.dev/docs/mill.md), not in
ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Not legal advice

This interpreter, its tests, and its example modules are not legal
advice.
